response.description: Ikea France, a subsidiary of the Ingka Group, has announced an internal restructuring that could affect up to 303 positions, primarily within its administrative functions across France, especially in Paris. The plan also includes the creation of 100 new roles. Of the 303 positions, 164 will be eliminated, 100 individual will be redeployed, and approximately 40 contracts be modified. The restructuring is driven by changes in the furniture market, accelerated digitalisation, and intensified competition. The aim is to simplify operations, shorten decision-making processes, and strengthen relationships with those in the field. The job saving plan negotiations will start in November and continue until March 2027. The trade unions CFDT and CGT, have engaged in negotiations. A CFDT representative criticised the decision as paradoxal in view of the company's finances. He also points out to the lack of actions regarding the rise of AI and the digital transition. This restructuring also takes place in a context where the relationship between management and employees is already strained, following the lack of social dialogue of July 2025 Ikea France 2026 - FR. The total workforce of Ikea France is over 12,000 employees. The ERM database has recorded several large-scale restructurings by Ikea, with the latest in Spain: IKEA 2026 - ES. Citation Eurofound (2026), Ikea, Internal restructuring in France, factsheet number 301330, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/301330. Flutter Entertainment, an Irish online gambling group, announced the dismissal of approximately 300 employees from its Betfair Romania Development software centre in Cluj-Napoca (Cluj County). The dismissal is part of a broader restructuring plan affecting up to 1,400 positions across the UK & Ireland division due to rising taxes. The changes will take effect shortly after the 20 October announcement, with additional cuts planned at Leeds, Dublin (see Flutter Ireland and Porto. The group has a workforce of 2,400 persons at its Cluj-Napoca site. MasterD, a Spanish training provider, has announced up to 231 job cuts in Spain affecting about 20 % of its workforce of roughly 1 200 employees in Spain. The restructuring aims to adapt the company’s operating model to changing student demand, requiring faster response and improved services. New processes and tools are being introduced, making some roles redundant. Unions have expressed strong opposition, citing high profitability and potential sale plans, and will mobilise to halt the layoffs. Negotiations with workers are scheduled to begin on the 4th of November 2026. MasterD is part of the Davante group, which includes more than 120 centres across Spain, Portugal and Italy. Citation Eurofound (2026), MasterD, Internal restructuring in Spain, factsheet number 301296, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/301296. Foxconn Slovakia, part of the Taiwanese Hon Hai Technology Group, has started recruiting new employees at its plant in Nitra, focusing on electrical engineering professions. Foxconn Slovakia did not officially specify the number of new jobs. According to an unnamed source from the company’s management, at least 300 positions are to be created. The company has opened the first engineering and technical positions for specialists with an electrical engineering background and plans to extend recruitment to production and assembly positions at a later stage. It emphasises vocational training and skills development in areas such as robotics and smart manufacturing. The company said it is responding to growing demand for AI infrastructure solutions and new business opportunities in this area. The recruitment follows a collective redundancy at the Nitra plant: in November 2025, the company notified the dismissal of 509 employees, and the first employees received notice in December 2025 Foxconn Slovakia. The plant produces consumer electronics, automotive components and other electrotechnical products. Citation Eurofound (2026), Foxconn Slovakia, Business expansion in Slovakia, factsheet number 301324, European Restructuring Monitor. The German automotive components manufacturer Mahle has announced a new Employment redundancy file (ERE) affecting 170 employees at its plant in Motilla del Palancar (Cuenca), representing approximately one third of its current workforce of 500. The proposal comes just one year after a previous restructuring, initially involving 550 proposed redundancies, which was subsequently reduced through negotiations with trade unions. Both Unions have strongly opposed the new plan, accusing Mahle of failing to fulfil its commitment to explore alternative industrial projects and secure the plant’s future. The unions have also criticised the limited progress achieved by the reindustrialisation working group established with the Spanish Ministry of Industry and the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha. Both unions have announced their intention to pursue measures to minimise job losses and defend the industrial future of the La Manchuela region. The company already experienced two previous restructing events in 2022 Mahle España 2022-ESand 2025 Mahle España 2025-ES, with a total of 343 and 506 redundancies, respectively Citation Eurofound (2026), Mahle España, Internal restructuring in Spain, factsheet number 301294, European Restructuring Monitor. Wollsdorf Components announced the closure of its production facility in Jalžabet, Varaždin County, Croatia, in October 2026. The closure follows declining demand for leather products in the European automotive industry and the company's deteriorating competitiveness. Employment contracts have been terminated for 285 workers, with employment expected to end by mid-December 2026. Production will be phased out by year-end. Negotiations could preserve 15-25 jobs under new ownership. The company, part of Austria's Wollsdorf Group, has operated in Croatia since 2013, manufacturing leather components for the automotive and aviation industries. Citation Eurofound (2026), Wollsdorf Components, Closure in Croatia, factsheet number 301312, European Restructuring Monitor. SHEIN, a Singaporean e-commerce and fashion retailer, plans to create 1,000 additional jobs at its European Logistics Centre near Wrocław, Poland. Further recruitment is planned in the coming months. The centre uses digital technologies, including robotic order-picking systems and automated sorting lines.The expansion is intended to further strengthen SHEIN’s logistics capacity for the European market. New opportunities will cover logistics, transport, supply-chain and warehouse operations, including customs clearance, project management, procurement, data analysis, inventory control, health and safety, automation maintenance and process optimisation. More than 200 Polish companies currently provide goods and services supporting SHEIN’s logistics activities. More than 3,000 jobs have already been created at the site SHEIN 2025 -PL Citation Eurofound (2026), SHEIN, Business expansion in Poland, factsheet number 301293, European Restructuring Monitor. Norwegian, a Norway-based airline, plans to dismiss 125 employees at its Copenhagen base: 55 pilots and 70 cabin crew. This represents around one-fifth of the approximately 630 flight crew in Copenhagen. As of October 2026, it is unknown when the dismissals will take effect, though the company aims to conclude the process quickly. The company cites insufficient winter demand and seasonal fluctuations in Copenhagen, while denying financial difficulties. The job losses have been announced as dismissals, but their final number and form depend on the outcome of the collective redundancy consultations. Consultations with employee representatives began on 19 October 2026, with three meetings scheduled. The union Flyvebranchens Personale Union (FPU) has demanded that the company mitigate the consequences for its members. Citation Eurofound (2026), Norwegian, Internal restructuring in Denmark, factsheet number 301299, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/301299. Avatel, a Spanish telecommunications operator owned by Inveready, has announced the dismissal of 444 staff positions from its current workforce of 1,325 employees in Spain. The layoffs, part of an internal restructuring prompted by worsening economic results and the return of subsidies linked to 5G rollout projects, are driven partly by accelerated digitalisation with AI systems replacing redundant roles. Unions have engaged in dialogue over the plan. Avatel has previously implemented similar collective dismissals in 2024 Avatel 2024-ES and 2026Avatel 2026-ES, with job redundancies of 674 and 302 jobs, respectively Citation Eurofound (2026), Avatel, Internal restructuring in Spain, factsheet number 301270, European Restructuring Monitor. Servinform, an Spanish company specialising in business process outsourcing (BPO), consultancy and customer services, has announced an Employment Redundancy File (ERE) potentially affecting around 430 employees, equivalent to approximately 10% of the 4,359 staff employed. According to trade union sources, 329 redundancies could occur in Seville, with additional employees affected in Madrid, Valencia, Granada, Barcelona, Las Palmas and Bizkaia. The company attributes the restructuring primarily to the loss of several major service contracts with Endesa, alongside increasing competitive pressures and organisational changes in the outsourcing sector. The formal consultation process with employee representatives is expected to begin shortly, with the final number of redundancies and compensation arrangements still subject to negotiation. Despite the restructuring, Servinform emphasises that its operations will continue normally, supported by recently renewed and newly secured contracts with public administrations and major corporate clients. Citation Eurofound (2026), Servinform, Internal restructuring in Spain, factsheet number 301271, European Restructuring Monitor. Carrefour Polska, the Polish subsidiary of the French retailer Carrefour, will make up to 210 employees redundant at four stores in the Bemowo shopping centre in Warsaw, Sieradz, Olsztyn and Bełchatów. The company notified the district labour office in Warsaw on 10 September 2026, and the process is due to be completed by December 2026. The company cites expiring leases and the persistent unprofitability of the stores, which recovery plans did not reverse, as part of a transformation plan launched in early 2025. Some employees will be offered transfers to other Carrefour stores or new roles within the company. Consultations with trade unions concluded on 30 September 2026. Carrefour Polska operates more than 700 stores in Poland. The previous restructuring recorded in the ERM was announced in January 2026.Carrefour Polska 2026 - PL Citation Eurofound (2026), Carrefour Polska, Closure in Poland, factsheet number 301276, European Restructuring Monitor. Länsförsäkringar, a Swedish insurance group, announced the potential dismissal of 400 employees across its subsidiaries as part of an extensive change programme launched in the spring of 2026 to streamline operations and cut costs. The restructuring aims to reduce expenses by at least two billion kronor (approx. €179 million), improve work practices, and secure long-term competitiveness. Job losses cover all affected subsidiaries except local county branches. The company has reported the process to the Employment Agency, as required, and trade union negotiations are ongoing. The Länsförsäkringar group has about 4000 employees. The whole Länsförsäkringar organisation, including the local county branches, currently employs around 10,200 staff. Citation Eurofound (2026), Länsförsäkringar, Internal restructuring in Sweden, factsheet number 301269, European Restructuring Monitor. Telia, a Swedish telecommunications operator, announced a reduction of around 900 jobs across its global operations, with the majority of potential cuts, approximately 280 positions, in Finland. With the restructuring, Telia aims to streamline its organisation and achieve savings of about 1 billion krona (roughly €89 million). The process is set to conclude by the end of 2026. The company attributes the changes to a need for organisational simplification and cost containment. In Finland, 355 roles are at risk of dismissal, while the company plans to open 75 new positions in Finland. In addition, around 50 roles would be transferred from the Group to Telia Finland. Planned reductions also include approximately 260 positions in Sweden, 150 in Norway, 110 in Lithuania and 100 in Estonia. Telia employs around 14,000 people worldwide, including approximately 2,500 in Finland. Kaufland, a German retail chain, announced the opening of two new hypermarkets in Galati (Galati County) and Satu Mare (Satu Mare County) on 8 October 2026. The move will create more than 140 jobs across both locations, boosting local employment. The stores, built on converted buildings, reflect the group’s sustainability strategy. The expansion is driven by the need to strengthen retail presence while adopting green initiatives such as energy-efficient infrastructure and waste segregation systems. Digital features—self-checkout machines and a mobile scanning service—also support the company’s digital transition agenda. Jobs will be created in both cities, with each hypermarket expected to add roughly half of the total new positions. Kaufland has over 157 000 employees worldwide and operates more than 200 stores in Romania, positioning it as a leading player in the national retail market. Walzengießerei Coswig, a German metal-casting company, announced the shutdown of its only foundry in Coswig, Saxony. The closure will eliminate about 170 jobs from the plant’s workforce by the end of November 2026. The decision follows years of low utilisation, the loss of customers, fierce competition and rising energy and metal costs that have made continued operation unsustainable. The company had filed for bankruptcy in November 2025. Bankruptcy proceedings under self-administration were initiated in February 2026. However, no investors were found. The job losses are concentrated entirely in Coswig. A social dialogue with the work council is underway regarding a potential severance plan, and IG Metall representatives have voiced concerns about the closure’s impact on workers. Following the closure announcement, a job fair was organised for affected employees, and the IHK began efforts to place the eight apprentices with alternative employers. Walzengießerei Coswig was part of the Dihag group, which operates around 10 comparable subsidiaries in the steel industry across Europe. EEW Special Pipe Constructions, a German manufacturer of components for offshore wind turbines, announced roughly 100 job cuts at its Rostock Überseehafen production plant in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. The layoffs are expected to be completed by the end of 2026. The decision was made because the company expects a limited utilization of its capacity up to and including 2028. This limited utilization is driven by a steep decline in offshore wind turbine orders, with no new projects awarded on German coasts in 2026. Moreover, wind farm expansions that have already been approved are also stalling due to rising costs. The company also faces intense competition from chinese suppliers, as preformed steel parts can enter the EU duty-free. The cut will only affect the production unit at the Rostock port site. There are currently around 1,000 employees working at the site in Rostock.100 employees are expected to leave the company by the end of 2026. Nidec, a Japanese manufacturer of electrical and mechatronic components for the automotive market, announced the shutdown of its production plant in Bietigheim-Bissingen, Baden-Württemberg. The closure will eliminate 116 production jobs by the end of 2027, while approximately 84 administrative employees will relocate to Stuttgart. The company cites the loss of a major customer from 2027 onwards as the main reason for the end to production. The decision also reflects an economic restructuring prompted by evolving market conditions and cost pressures within the automotive components sector. The layoffs amount to 116 jobs, all in the production unit in Bietigheim-Bissingen. The relocation of 84 administrative functions to Stuttgart remains internal and has already been organised. IG Metall and the works council are actively engaged, demanding transparent explanations of the financial rationale and exploring alternatives. Nidec, part of a global group with roughly 104,000 employees worldwide, faces the challenge of balancing efficiency with social responsibility as it moves forward with this closure. Citation Eurofound (2026), Nidec, Closure in Germany, factsheet number 301263, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/301263. OP-Pohjola, a Finnish financial services group, announced cooperation negotiations that could eliminate up to 554 posts and establish approximately 277 new roles across its insurance and retail banking operations. The negotiations cover approximately 2,340 employees. Insurance negotiations began on 6 October 2026 and retail banking negotiations are scheduled to begin on 12 October. Both are expected to last at least three weeks. The changes reflect shifting customer behaviour, increased competition and regulatory changes affecting the division of work between central functions and local cooperative banks. Tasks previously performed centrally have returned to local banks. The new roles would be offered to employees at risk of dismissal. OP-Pohjola employs approximately 15,000 people. Ryanair, an Irish low-cost airline, announced in October 2026 the recruitment of 250 employees for its Customer Service Escalation Center in Warsaw, Poland, revised upward from an initial figure of 200. The expansion responds to the growth of the airline’s operations in Poland, one of its key markets alongside Ireland. The centre handles cases escalated beyond the company’s artificial intelligence systems, which deal with routine enquiries. The centre provides support in English, Polish, French and Spanish, and operates in shifts. Staff are employed on contracts of employment and receive additional benefits. The company expects the team to grow to 300 in the following months. Alicja Wójcik-Gołębiowska, Ryanair’s communications director for Central and Eastern Europe, stated that shift scheduling is intended to allow employees to combine the work with other commitments, such as studies. Aspang (Neunkirchen) and Pernitz (Wiener Neustadt-Land) will close, while other sites such as Ternitz, Schwechat, Gloggnitz, Grimmenstein, Krumbach, Bruck and Thomasberg are being restructured but without confirmed job cuts. Union GPA Niederösterreich has begun negotiations with management for a social plan to mitigate the impact. Breyden, a German metal-casting company, has announced the closure of its iron-casting site in Ueckermünde in Mecklenburg West-Pomerania, which will eliminate roughly 300 jobs by 31 December 2026. The factory produces cast components for automotive manufacturers. Breyden cites sustained economic pressures due to competition from Asia, a falling market demand and an insufficient utilization of its capacity as the driving reasons for the shutdown. All job losses are concentrated in Ueckermünde. While some workers may be offered transfer to nearby factories, operated by other companies, such as in Torgelow, no concrete relocation plan has been confirmed. The company will negotiate a social plan with its works council. The IG Metall has criticised the very sudden closure and has announced to participate in negotiations with the company. Breyden’s workforce total and future site openings remain unspecified. The company has around 14,000 employees in Germany across five different sites located in Breidenbach, Neunkirchen, Immenhausen, Altenburg and Ueckermünde. The closure affects all the employees of the site in Ueckermünde. The company had to previously close one of its sites in Lollar (Hesse) which led to the layoff of 230 employees in 2025 Breyden 2025 - DE. Citation Eurofound (2026), Breyden, Closure in Germany, factsheet number 301220, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/301220. Aldi Süd, a German discount retailer, announced the elimination of about 150 jobs at its headquarters in Mülheim an der Ruhr. The cuts target the Human Resources and Customer Interaction marketing departments. The timeline of the restructuring has not been communicated. The reduction is driven by rising costs in the discount sector, increasing IT requirements, and evolving consumer habits. The use of AI in customer communications is also likely to lead to job cuts. All job losses are concentrated at the Mülheim headquarters; employees were offered termination agreements. Around 100 layoffs affect the Human Ressources unit. Another 40 to 50 layoffs affect the customer interaction unit.The company also plans to shift certain marketing functions to Hungary as part of a broader cost-saving strategy. Aldi Süd notes that all affected employees are provided with legal support. Aldi Süd employs roughly 50,000 people in Germany, with around 2,000 staff at its Mülheim an der Ruhr base. The company operates around 2000 stores throughout Germany. Earlier this year the company had already announced a reduction of 1,250 employees in its digital unit in Mülheim an der Ruhr Aldi Süd 2025 - DE. F-Secure, a Finnish cybersecurity firm, announced plans to reduce up to 58 roles in Finland as part of a new operating model involving up to 145 role reductions worldwide, including 87 outside Finland. Negotiations began on 6th October 2026 and are expected to last about six weeks. The new operating model is expected to take effect on 1 January 2027. According to the company, artificial intelligence is one of the reasons behind the restructuring as it transforms the company's work, market and the threats it combats. The restructuring aims to sharpen customer focus, accelerate AI-driven services, and deliver estimated annual cost savings of €13 million while investing in growth. F-Secure employs nearly 600 persons worldwide, while the Finnish parent company employed 262 people in 2025. F-Secure, a Finnish cybersecurity firm, has announced an overhaul of its operating model that will lead to up to 145 job cuts worldwide. The company plans to reduce positions by at most 58 in Finland, as recorded in the ERM Events database F-Secure 2026 - FI and at most 87 in other locations. The restructuring is driven largely by a digital transition agenda: F-Secure aims to embed AI across its organization to anticipate and respond swiftly to evolving product and service demands, while simultaneously expanding growth-stage offerings and strengthening profitability. These adjustments are part of a broader shift toward a leaner, customer-centric structure that seeks to deliver faster results without sacrificing security expertise. The company currently employs 597 staff globally and its present in 25 across the world; notably in Europe, Africa and Middle East. Paul Köster GmbH, a German manufacturer of specialty machinery focused on sealing inspection, assembly and automation technologies, announced the elimination of 90 jobs at its Medebach site, leaving 212 positions intact, including all training contracts. This reduction is part of an insolvency restructuring that is scheduled to conclude by January 2027. The company was prompted to enter an insolvency restructuring following a sharp decline in automotive industry orders, rising input costs and several customer insolvencies. All the job cuts are concentrated at the site in Medebach. The aim is to stabilize operations while preserving the Medebach plant. Affected employees are transferred to a transfer agency and are provided with additional training to help them find new employment. IG Metall has been involved in advisory discussions with management. The family business had around 300 employees at the opening of proceedings, leaving the company with a workforce of roughly 200 after the layoffs. This means that every third employee is layed off. The company only has a site in Medebach. Citation Eurofound (2026), Paul Köster, Internal restructuring in Germany, factsheet number 301214, European Restructuring Monitor. Szpital Miejski w Miastku, a municipal hospital in Pomorskie Voivodeship, Poland, entered bankruptcy proceedings in 2026. Collective redundancies cover around 180 employees on contracts of employment. The redundancies will affect nurses, midwives, physiotherapists, and administrative/support personnel. The hospital accumulated debts exceeding PLN 40 million and lost its medical staff. The National Health Fund also imposed a penalty of PLN 13.2 million over irregularities in the settlement of procedures carried out by an external company. The healthcare facility progressively suspended its departments: internal medicine from 1 July 2026, surgery and intensive care from 17 July, and the operating theatre and diagnostic units including X-ray and computed tomography from 1 August. Its contracts with the National Health Fund lapsed on 1 and 4 August. The Wojewódzki Szpital Specjalistyczny in Słupsk offered employment to the hospital’s nurses. The Powiatowe Centrum Pomocy Rodziny in Bytów and Miastko commune offered support to employees and their families. The hospital is owned by Miastko commune, which had recently transferred PLN 5 million to it. Two emergency medical teams remain stationed in Miastko and patients requiring hospitalisation are directed to Bytów, Kościerzyna, Chojnice, Słupsk and Człuchów. Citation Eurofound (2026), City Hospital Miastko, Bankruptcy in Poland, factsheet number 301253, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/301253. Following the cessation of Sareb’s activities, the Spanish Government has confirmed the collective dismissal of 247 employees. Sareb (Sociedad de Gestión de Activos Procedentes de la Reestructuración Bancaria), often referred to as Spain’s “bad bank”, was created in 2012 during the financial crisis to acquire and manage distressed property assets and real estate loans transferred from rescued Spanish banks. Its role was to gradually dispose of these assets and stabilise the banking system. Trade unions have challenged the decision before the courts. Trade Unions accuse the Government of opting for redundancies to reduce labour costs while simultaneously recruiting and training new staff to perform similar functions within a new created Institutions called Casa 47. The dispute takes place against the backdrop of Spain’s housing crisis and the broader reorganisation of the state’s public housing policy. Quantum Real, a Polish logistics and industrial property developer, has started construction of a warehouse in Gliwice, which is expected to create around 200 jobs. The 43,000 m² facility is scheduled to open in the first quarter of 2027. The energy-efficient warehouse will feature extensive cold storage and dry logistics areas designed to support food distribution from Mediterranean suppliers. Bosch, a German automotive supplier, has announced that it will be cutting up to 900 jobs at its Nürenberg site until the end of 2029. As a supplier to the internal combustion engine industry, Bosch is affected by the shift towards electric mobility. In addition, Bosch is facing increasing competition from China and declining sales. Bosch also cited the slower-than-expected development of the European hydrogen market, which has reduced production volumes and plant utilisation. The company said it intends to seek socially responsible solutions for the workforce reduction. There are currently 1,800 jobs at the site in Nürenberg, half of which will be layed off. The cuts come in addition to previously announced group-wide workforce reductions of 13,000 jobs worldwide Bosch 2025 - WO, including 8,610 job cuts in Germany Bosch 2025 - DE. Accenture will recruit around 100 professionals and open a new innovation centre dedicated to the development and deployment of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in Barcelona. The facility is intended to help private companies and public administrations adopt AI systems capable of autonomously executing complex tasks, moving beyond the capabilities of traditional generative AI tools. The new centre will provide demonstration environments, solution design services and technical advisory support, enabling organisations at different stages of digital maturity to evaluate and implement AI-driven automation. The expansion will create demand for specialists in artificial intelligence, data science, software engineering, automation, cybersecurity and digital transformation, as well as experts in AI governance and regulatory compliance. By combining technology and business expertise, Accenture aims to position Barcelona as a strategic hub for the practical deployment of agentic AI, supporting the transition from pilot projects to large-scale implementation across multiple sectors. The Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), a German public broadcaster, announced the cancellation of 76 programms and plans to reduce staff positions by roughly 133 through retirement attrition by 2030. The cuts target its television, podcast, and social media units across Germany and are set to be fully implemented by 31/12/2027 for program cancellations and by 31/12/2030 for the workforce reductions. WDR attributes the restructuring to shifting media consumption patterns, rising costs, and an uncertain funding environment, prompting a strategic move toward digital platforms. The change also involves relocating production resources toward technology-oriented roles. Job losses are largely achieved through attrition—positions that become vacant via retirement will not be refilled—amounting to about 133 positions. No explicit location breakdown is provided beyond the national scope. However, all of the broadcasters sites are dispersed accross North Rhine-Westphalia. The union Verdi has criticized the measures but there are no reported negotiations with social partners regarding the restructuring. WDR employs approximately 4 000 staff members. The broadcaster intends to continue operating its core digital services and maintain some physical facilities while reducing office space by about 100 000 m² by end-2028. Fujikura Automotive Romania, an automotive component manufacturer, announced that 309 persons will be dismissed by 31 October 2026 at Dej factory (Cluj County). The measure is part of a process to adjust production capacity, as the financial outlook is not very positive for the fiscal year April 2026–March 2027. The notice sent to employees states that a decline in turnover is anticipated, given that the company’s main project has reached the end of its life cycle. The restructuring document also indicates a reduction of 45 employees in the indirect production staff, whilst a further 16 posts in the TESA department are to be made redundant. The move follows declining demand and is an internal capacity adjustment rather than a full closure. All affected employees will receive collective dismissal under Romanian law, with the County Employment Agency (AJOFM) Cluj offering placement support. Delivery Hero, a German online-food delivery and technology platform firm, is relocating its tech unit, called Pandora, from Berlin to Singapore by the end of 2026. Around 200 employees are affected. The relocation follows Uber’s announced acquisition of large parts of Delivery Hero and aims to centralise technology operations and reduce the number of jobs in Berlin. Delivery Hero's tech unit provides the technical infrastructure for online-food delivery platforms that operate in European and Asian markets. Originally, all of Pandora's 400 employees were to be moved to Singapore at once. However, the Singaporean government requires that a certain percentage of the company's workforce must be made up of local employees. Therefore, half of the tech unit will have to stay in Berlin until the integration of Delivery Hero into Uber is finished. No explicit job cuts or other measures have been reported, though further workforce reductions in Berlin are possible in the long run. The remaining 200 positions may also be moved to Singapore at a later point in time. The works council has expressed cautious support but raised concerns about potential staffing changes. No definitive completion date concerning the remaining 200 employees is provided and no further phases are mentioned. The restructuring only affects the copany's headquarters in Berlin. Delivery Hero has around 40,000 employees in 65 different countries. 3,000 employees work at the headqarters in Berlin. This includes Pandora's 400 employees of which 200 will definitely be outsourced. Ardo Austria Frost GmbH, the Austrian subsidiary of Belgium-based Ardo Group, announced the closure of its frozen vegetable production and packaging plant in Groß-Enzersdorf, Lower Austria, by the end of August 2027. The restructuring affects 190 employees and around 50 agency workers. The company cited the site's lack of economic competitiveness, pointing to higher energy, labour and raw-material costs in Austria than at other European production locations. Production for the Austrian market will be transferred within Ardo’s European network. Ardo will continue supplying the Austrian market through other European sites. The company is a key processor of vegetables grown in the Marchfeld region. The closure will affect the entire Groß-Enzersdorf facility. In addition to direct job losses, around 270 supplying farmers and the producer organisation ETG, representing approximately 500 vegetable farms, are expected to be affected. The trade union PRO-GE called for measures to preserve jobs, a social plan is under preparation. The closure is part of a wider restructuring programme across Austria and Belgium, involving a total of 227 job losses: Ardo 2026 - EU. Embargos a lo Bestia, a Spanish retailer specialising in discounted furniture, appliances and home goods, announced the loss of approximately 270 jobs as it shut down all its physical stores across Spain. The chain’s decline stemmed from razor-thin margins, sharp sales falls, and unsustainable debt that thwarted attempts to restructure through investment or an online focus. In early August 2026 the company commenced a progressive closure of its outlets and on-line store and subsequently filed for voluntary insolvency, leading to a liquidation process overseen by AB Global Concursal SL and the opening of an Employment redundancy File (ERE) affecting all its workers. The liquidation will clear remaining obligations with workers, banks and suppliers, signalling the end of Embargos a lo Bestia’s retail operations. GSK, a British pharmaceutical company, announced in September 2026 the reduction of more than 500 posts at its Poznań site in Wielkopolskie. The company decided to transfer part of the activity to India and to consolidate some support services outside Poland, under a three-year programme presented in July to simplify operations and concentrate resources, supporting a sales target above GBP 40 billion by 2031. The posts affected are in information technology, a support function within the site, rather than in pharmaceutical production. No timeline for implementing the job losses has been announced. NSZZ Solidarność, whose company organisation is chaired by Hieronim Marut, is entering negotiations on departure terms. GSK states that supporting employees and cooperating with the unions is its priority. Poznań will remain the location of one of GSK's two multifunctional Global Capability Centres. Warsteiner Brauerei, a German brewery based in Warstein, announced it will cut 125 full-time positions by the end of the year. The job losses are concentrated at the Warstein site. The restructuring is driven by a challenging market environment and declining beer sales in Germany, combined with cost-saving objectives. Warsteiner is simultaneously investing in new technology such as a de-alcoholisation plant and building a wind turbine expected to supply half of its electricity needs, signalling a green transition that supports the overall strategy. The cuts involve about 50 jobs that will not be replaced after retirements or short-term contract expirations, and roughly 80 further roles for which socially responsible solutions are being sought with the works council. These solutions may include transfers or training opportunities. The Union NGG criticizes the layoffs and claims that they contradict recent assurances from management according to which jobs at the Warstein site would be secured. There are around 725 employees at the Warstein site of which around 125 are affected by reductions. The site will continue to operate. Groupe Schiever, a French retail logistics group, is expanding its operations by constructing a new warehouse in Magny (Yonne). The project will create 100 jobs in hiring in logistics. The increase in transport flows is expected to require at least 20 additional drivers. The company also expects the development to generate up to 400 jobs over five years. The project is being supported by U Logistics, the logistics company of the food distributor Coopérative U. The recruitment will include several positions, including order pickers, forklift operators, foremen and managerial roles. Construction began in March 2026, while the 54,000 m² warehouse is scheduled to become operational in June 2027. The expansion aims to streamline supply chains, cut transportation distances by an estimated 700 000 km per year, and reduce CO₂ emissions by 2,500 tonnes annually, reflecting a strong green-transition strategy. Groupe Schiever employs over 7,000 workers across the world. Citation Eurofound (2026), Schiever, Business expansion in France, factsheet number 301250, European Restructuring Monitor. Cims, an Italian construction, facility management and environmental services cooperative, announced plans that could result in approximately 70 job cuts among its workforce of around 300 employees in Borgo Tossignano, Bologna province. The planned workforce reduction, follows a deterioration in the cooperative's financial position and ongoing liquidity constraints. The company intends to apply for social protection measures during the restructuring process, while details regarding the number of employees affected, possible redundancies, transfers of activities and other workforce adjustment measures remain under discussion with employee representatives. Trade unions CGIL, CISL and UIL expressed strong concern following meetings with management, citing the absence of a new recovery plan and warning of potential insolvency risks should creditors initiate legal action. The unions have called for the urgent activation of a regional crisis task force and urged local authorities and Legacoop to support measures aimed at safeguarding employment and mitigating the social impact of the restructuring. Further discussions with the company's president are expected in the coming days. Mubea, a German automotive parts supplier, announced the reduction of approximately 200 positions at its Daaden/Weitefeld plant in Rhineland-Palatinate. The cut is set to conclude by the end of 2028. The restructuring responds to changes in customer purchasing decisions, heightened cost pressure, cost-increasing EU regulations, US tariff impacts, and a strategy to strengthen competitiveness through automation, digitalisation and the use of AI-supported processes. All affected staff are concentrated at the Daaden/Weitefeld site. 200 out of 600 employees at the site will be layed off. The company has announced that the layoffs will be carried out in a socially responsible manner through severance and bridge pension programmes. In addition, the company searches for job opportunities in its other locations that could be filled by the affected employees. Mubea employs roughly 17,200 people worldwide across 70 sites. Mubea has about 4,500 employees in Germany. The site in Daaden/Weitefeld already faced layoffs in the last two years: Mubea 2024 - DE. Sky Deutschland was acquired by the RTL Group and merged with another German media company, RTL Deutschland in June 2026. RTL Deutschland announced that it will cut around 500 jobs by the end of 2027, with the majority of cuts expected to take place as early as 2026. Geographically, the cuts affect job sites in Munich and Cologne. The job cuts are implemented following the acquisition of Sky Deutschland and are aimed at optimizing costs and structures, particularly by eliminating duplicate functions and streamlining program planning. As of September 2026, it is still unclear how the cuts will be distributed among the different locations, Sky Deutschland and RTL Deutschland. Expiring contracts will not be renewed and open positions will not be filled. The measure will be implemented in close cooperation with the working councils. The cuts were denunciated by the services union Ver.di. RTL has more than 5,300 employees while Sky Deutschland has around 2,170. Previously RTL Deutschland RTL Deutschland has already cut around 600 jobs in 2025. Himolla, a German furniture manufacturer, announced the elimination of 175 positions at its production plant in Taufkirchen (Bayern) following an insolvency filing in June 2026 and subsequent reorganisation under self-management from September 1, 2026. 540 jobs will remain at the site in Taufkirchen. Jobs in final production and related fields, as well as in administration, are affected. The restructuring is driven by a sharp decline in the furniture market, weak construction activity, and intense competition from low-wage producers, prompting cost cuts to safeguard the business’s long-term viability. Negotiations are underway with the works council over a social plan to mitigate the impact of the job losses. The 175 jobs are lost because the final assembly division in Taufkirchen will be closed and relocated to Slovakia and Hungary. Himolla has more than 2000 employees across multiple sites in Germany and other countries. Robert Bosch Production Slovakia, a subsidiary of the German industrial giant Bosch Group, announced the permanent closure of its factory in Bernolákovo, Slovakia. The move will eliminate 148 jobs at the plant's repair and diagnostics unit for automotive alternators. Production is slated to finish by 31 March 2027, after which the site will be sold and the legal entity dissolved. The decision stems from rising competition, declining global vehicle demand, and a need to consolidate smaller, highly specialised production sites into larger existing facilities – in this case, an existing Bosch plant in Pećinci, Serbia. The company stated that Serbia did not provide any investment support or tax incentives in connection with the relocation, and that the decision was based purely on strategic and economic considerations. Bosch has already informed employee representatives, followed by the affected employees themselves, about the planned closure. The company intends to negotiate severance terms and a social plan with employee representatives, aiming for what it describes as the most socially responsible solution possible; specific terms have not yet been disclosed. Ouest-France, a French media company headquartered in Rennes, announced the elimination of 156 positions, 116 in their editorial staff. The company is restructuring due to the continuing decrease in revenue, caused by the decrease in sales of paper journals and advertisement income. No firings are planned, but rely on natural departures and end of fixed-term contracts. The job cuts are set to conclude by the end of 2028. Digital transition, driven by the implementation of AI tools for efficiency, is cited as a key factor underpinning the restructuring. Prisma Peremarket, a Finnish retail company under the SOK Group, announced a reduction of 67 jobs in its support unit in Estonia on 16 September 2026. This accounts for about 10 % of its total workforce of 655 employees in Estonia, with the notice period ranging from one to three months. The cuts are limited to the support functions and do not affect the company's retail network. The restructuring follows the sale of Prisma Peremarket to Coop Eesti Keskühistu and aims to streamline operations under a new ownership structure, ensuring greater competitiveness in Estonia's tight-margin retail market. While specific details on how employees will be dismissed are not provided, the company has pledged to offer alternative roles where possible and is cooperating with the Estonian Employment Service to provide job-search assistance. The final number of redundancies will be determined within the process of transforming from Prisma to Coop. Afpa, the French public agency in vocational training, announced that 788 job cuts will take place until 2029, as well as 79 job modifications and 400 recruitments. This internal restructuring aims to limit the losses of the national agency which has been facing deficits due to decreasing turnover and high maintenance costs. Indeed, it is less competitive than its private counterparts, who are gaining competitiveness in public procurement. The agency therefore aims to resolve this issue in the following three years. In the Grand Est region, 139 employees will lose their jobs. The plan also involves closing several centres, notably those in Verdun (Meuse) and Saint-Dizier (Haute-Marne). The recruitment of 400 new positions will take place in commercial development and the opening of 13 additional sites. Several trade unions, such as CGT, FO and Sud, have voiced their concerns. Afpa’s total workforce stands at approximately 5,410 before the restructuring. Atlantic Copper has officially inaugurated CirCular, its new electronic waste recycling plant in Huelva, follo-wing an investment of €550 million. The facility will create 350 highly qualified Jobs and process up to 60,000 tonnes of waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) annually, positioning Spain among the few countries worldwide with advanced industrial capacity to recover strategic metals from electronic waste. The plant will process pre-treated materials to recover valuable metals such as copper, gold, silver, palladium, platinum, tin and nickel using innovative smelting technology. The project has been recognised as a strategic initiative by the European Union since 2023 and is expected to make a significant contribution to European recycling targets and the security of critical raw material supplies. Atlantic Copper estimates that CirCular will increase its annual turnover by 20–30%, while reinforcing the circular economy and reducing Europe’s dependence on imported raw materials. The company is already planning a second expansion pha-se to further strengthen its recycling capabilities and support the growing demand for critical materials used in the energy transition and digital technologies. Ericsson, a Swedish telecommunications and information technology company, announced that 131 jobs are expected to be cut at its research and development operations in Genoa, Italy. The planned workforce reduction affects the entire Optical R&D unit and part of another R&D department involved in advanced network technologies and infrastructure. The restructuring is linked to the continuing difficulties affecting the Italian telecommunications market. The procedure involves 56 employees, 64 managers and 11 executives. Trade unions have called for discussions with the company and public authorities and urged measures to safeguard employment, while local, regional and national political representatives have requested institutional involvement in the case. This is part of a wider worldwide restructuring Ericsson 2026- WO. Updated, 05/10/2026 Ericsson has withdrawn the planned dismissal of 131 employees in Genoa and has launched voluntary and mutually agreed exit procedures. Italian luxury yacht manufacturer The Italian Sea Group (TISG) has announced 270 potential job cuts affecting its workforce at the Marina di Carrara shipyard in Tuscany, Italy. This follows a severe financial crisis linked to significant cost overruns on yacht construction contracts. This has led the company to enter a court-supervised crisis settlement procedure and seek a new investor through a competitive sale process. Instead of immediately implementing redundancies, the company and its stakeholders have agreed to a six-month solidarity contract, pending approval by the Florence Court and the Ministry of Labour. This contract involves reducing working hours, with the reductions to be shared among employees. Fim, Fiom and Uilm reported that the company had accepted union requests regarding advance payments, rotation arrangements, accrual of entitlements, leave treatment and consultation with workers' representatives on the management of the solidarity scheme. Citation Eurofound (2026), Italian Sea Group, Internal restructuring in Italy, factsheet number 301096, European Restructuring Monitor. Moelven Byggmodul AB, a Swedish manufacturer of wooden module constructions, has announced a layoff of 57 employees due to weak demand. In mid-September 2026, Moelven Byggmodul announced that 65 employees in manufacturing and 15 white-collar workers were subject to potential redundancies. The notice was a consequence of weak demand in the construction industry and means that one of the two production lines in Säffle will be shut down. Following trade union negotiations, the redundancy of employees within manufacturing was lowered to 57 with a notice period of four months. Negotiations concerning white-collar staff have not yet been finalised. The decision follows a period when the company restarted and then had to pause the production line after low orders. Management indicated that market conditions remain fragile but anticipates future opportunities as construction activity stabilises. Aerospacelab, a Belgian aerospace firm based in Marcinelle, announced the creation of approximately 500 jobs, after winning a €2.4 billion contract for the EU satellite network Iris². The company will grow its workforce from about 500 to roughly 1 000 employees at its new 16 000 m² satellite plant, making it Europe's largest satellite factory. All new jobs will be located in Marcinelle and the expansion will conclude by the end of 2029. The growth is driven by a major EU space programme investment that positions Aerospacelab at the forefront of satellite technology and fulfills the contractual requirement to produce 264 out of 348 satellites for the Iris² network. The project supports Europe's strategic autonomy in satellite communications and aligns with high-tech industry development. MaiaSpace, a French space industry company and subsidiary of ArianeGroup, announced the creation of 160 jobs at its new Maia Factory in Vernon, Eure. The plant will produce rocket components for launch vehicles to be transported to Le Havre before final assembly in French Guiana. The expansion is part of France’s national strategy to strengthen space sovereignty and meet future launch demand by 2032, aiming to conduct 20 launches per year with 25–30 stages produced annually.The project forms part of France's strategy to strengthen national and European sovereignty in access to space and to support future civilian and military satellite launches. The new facility will add to MaiaSpace's workforce, which has grown from around 20 employees at its founding to roughly 400 today. Previously, Maiaspace was mentioned in the ERM Database with a business expasion in the same site, at Vernon, with 160 new job positions created. GlaxoSmithKline (GSK), a British multinational pharmaceutical company, announced the closure of its Dresden plant in Germany, resulting in approximately 650 job cuts. Production will cease by September 2027, with the facility fully wound down by summer 2028. The restructuring is driven by GSK’s decision to concentrate vaccine production at a Canadian site and to eliminate excess capacity amid declining demand for traditional vaccines. Workers, represented by the works council and supported by the pharma-bio trade union IGBCE, have expressed strong opposition and plan to contest the decision. Regional and European political representatives also called for efforts to preserve pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity at the site. GSK employs 66,800 people in 70 countries and operates 33 production sites. In Germany, GSK reports 2.700 employees at five sites. IONOS, a subsidiary of the German internet services company United Internet, announced the reduction of around 450 full-time positions. Around half of these job cuts will take place in Germany. As of 24 September 2026, the other affected countries had not yet been announced. United Internet announced the reduction of about 800 full-time positions across its subsidiaries IONOS and 1&1 Versatel in Germany. The restructuring is driven by a strategic shift toward artificial-intelligence products and the expansion of the cloud business, aiming to fund new AI-driven services rather than improve margins. Digital transition drives the decision, as automation and efficiency gains will finance the costly transformation. All job cuts are being implemented through voluntary programmes and age-based retirements rather than direct dismissals. IONOS employs around 3,800 people worldwide, including 2,008 employees in Germany. The restructuring was announced on 10 September 2026, with no completion date specified. Veolia Energia S.A., a French-owned energy and district heating company operating in Poland, announced a restructuring affecting 595 employees in the Mazowieckie region, primarily in Warsaw. The job reductions were notified to the Regional Labour Office in Warsaw and are scheduled to be implemented by the end of September 2026. Separately, Veolia Energia Łódź stated that notices issued to employees relate to changes in employment terms under a group-wide job evaluation system rather than planned redundancies. The company indicated that the process is being implemented in consultation with employee representatives, although employees rejecting the new terms may ultimately leave the company. Booksy, a Polish technology startup operating in the beauty and wellness sector, announced in September a reduction of roughly 200 positions, about 20% of its workforce, across all markets where it operates, including Poland, the United States, and Spain. The layoffs are part of an AI-first transformation strategy aimed at simplifying organizational structures and focusing on core markets and self-service tools. This internal restructuring is expected to streamline teams for faster deployment of artificial intelligence solutions, without affecting ongoing hiring of new specialists in AI roles. The restructuring was announced publicly by the company’s management. Booksy previously carried out significant job reductions in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. It serves more than 200,000 businesses globally, with its largest markets including the United States, Poland and Spain. The company remains profitable. ÖBB, an Austrian railway operator, has opened a new maintenance and service hall for its double-decker Cityjet and Railjet trains in Vienna’s Floridsdorf district. The facility on Angerer Straße will employ about 150 workers and became fully operational on 10 September 2026. MBDA, a French defence company, announced the creation of 300 new jobs through the opening of a new site in Loiret and further expansion of its Selles-Saint-Denis plant. The firm will has committed to an investment envelope of €230 million for the Salamandre project, which includes two phases inaugurated on September 2026. The expansion is driven by geopolitical considerations that underscore France’s need for missile sovereignty and defence capability, as highlighted by MBDA’s leadership. The transformation will also incorporate modern digital manufacturing processes to enhance efficiency and resilience in the industry. Job creation is focused at the Loiret department level, with Selles-Saint-Denis hosting the full assembly line and the new facility expected to add capacity for future missile production. MBDA, jointly owned by Airbus, BAE Systems, and Leonardo, is a global defence leader. The company operates in France, Italy, Germany, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Previously in the ERM Database, MBDA was mentioned in another hiring campaign in France, in 2025, with 250 new job positions. Revoz, a car manufacturer owned by the French company Renault, will hire 300 new employees to produce the Dacia Spring, the second model powered exclusively by electricity. The job gains are driven by increased demand for electric vehicles and the introduction of a second production shift. This move aims to double daily production capacity to meet market needs. The 300 new positions include production line workers as well as research and development engineering staff. Revoz is currently producing the electric Twingo and is now starting production of the second Dacia Spring model, for which the company will hire 300 workers for the second shift. The second shift will be gradually introduced to reach roughly 600 vehicles per day by year-end. New hires will include production line workers as well as engineering staff for research and development. Management stated that the company is looking for production workers through the Employment Service and recruitment agencies. Nedri Spanstaal, a Dutch producer of prestressing steel and industrial wire, plans to close its production site in Blerick, Limburg, by the end of 2026, putting all 121 jobs at the site at risk. The company has faced a deterioration in its financial position, with lower investment by customers, reduced housing construction, US tariffs on steel and high energy prices cited as contributing factors; its turnover reportedly fell to €70 million in 2025 and it recorded a €3.2 million loss. The proposed closure must still be considered by the works council. A Trade Union FNV representative said the union intends to discuss the consequences with employees and, if the closure proceeds, seek support for workers to move into other employment or retraining, involving the parent group. Nedri has operated for around a century and produces specialised steel wire used in applications including bridges, wind energy, railway systems and construction. BrainRocket, an Israeli-owned technology firm, announced the shutdown of its Limassol offices in Cyprus and offered relocation packages to many employees. The company, which once employed around 1 500 staff locally, saw more than 1 000 affected by the restructuring as it moved most operations to Valencia and Malta. The move was driven by a strategic decision to consolidate resources abroad while maintaining a reduced presence in Cyprus. Employees were instructed to work remotely or accept relocation, with many choosing to relocate to Spain. The closure of physical premises marked the end of BrainRocket’s large-scale activity on the island. While the company did not formally confirm a full exit from Cyprus, the removal of its signage and cessation of office operations suggest that it has ceased substantial local operations. The restructuring reflects broader trends of tech firms relocating workforces across borders to optimise talent and infrastructure. La Poste, the French national postal operator, announced cutting 110 jobs until the end of 2027 in its administrative and management functions. The layoff aim to reduce costs of La Poste and guarantee the long-term financial autonomy of the company. Management has stated that while the new services have not been sufficient to cover La Poste's growing costs, service quality will be maintained, and the customer service sector will not be impacted by the layoffs. The changes will affect employees across France. Trade unions have expressed concern and called for alternatives such as redeployment and retraining before any dismissals are enacted. La Poste has several large restructurings recorded on the ERM database, primarily in France, and its last mention was a hiring campaign for 190 vacancies in Perpignan (Occitanie) La Poste 2025 - FR. Wizz Air, a Hungarian low-cost airline, announced the elimination of 172 positions in its Romanian operations, affecting staff at the Bucharest, Craiova, Cluj, and Iași bases. The workforce of 1892 employees will see about 10% of roles cut, with reductions expected between October and November 2026. The restructuring is driven by high fuel costs, inflationary pressure, weakening demand, and increased competition. All affected employees hold execution roles, including pilots, copilots, and cabin crew. Dismissals will be collective, following performance and seniority criteria, with no voluntary measures reported. The cuts are confined to Romania, without cross-border impact. Future plans include opening a new base at Brașov later in 2026, which will not affect the current cuts. WKW Hungary, the Hungarian subsidiary of WKW Group, a German automotive supplier, has announced the closure of its plant in Győr, Hungary, resulting in 470 job losses. The shutdown is scheduled to begin on the beginning of September 2026 and will be completed by end of December 2026. The subsidiary will be dissolved without a legal successor. The decision follows sustained order cancellations, a consequence of the automotive sector reeling from mounting challenges, making the continued operation of the plant unviable. Management has pledged to provide employees with monthly loyalty bonuses equivalent to half their monthly wages until production ends, in recognition of their good work performance. Local authorities and the union have begun discussions about how to facilitate new employment opportunities for the workers made redundant. LOT Aircraft Maintenance Services (LOTAMS), a Polish aviation maintenance and repair company, opened its new RZE2 maintenance base at Rzeszów-Jasionka Airport in September 2026 following a three-year investment project. The expansion is expected to create around 250 highly skilled positions, mainly for aircraft maintenance personnel and technical support staff in the Podkarpackie region. The recruitment process is ongoing. The investment was undertaken to increase maintenance capacity and to support anticipated growth in airline fleets. The new jobs at the Rzeszów-Jasionka facility include aircraft mechanics, engineers, inspectors and other technical specialists. Recruitment began before the base opened and continues as operations expand. Additional indirect employment may arise among regional suppliers and service providers linked to the aviation sector. LOTAMS employs nearly 2,000 people and provides aircraft maintenance services for commercial and military operators. The company continues to operate its existing facilities, including its Warsaw sites and the earlier RZE1 operation at Rzeszów-Jasionka. The Wellbeing Services County of North Savo (Pohjois-Savon hyvinvointialue), a Finnish public health care region, announced the reduction of 275 jobs across its services as a result of cooperation negotiations. The cuts comprise 50 direct dismissals and 2225 other measures that include retirements, termination of fixed-term contracts, position closures and unfilled vacancies. Units affected span personnel services, family and disability support, elderly care, administration, strategy development, financial services, property management, rescue services and special assistance. The restructuring is driven by fiscal constraints aimed at securing €11.6 million in savings for the next year, following a period of budget tightening. The negotiations ended in August 2026 in disagreement. All five staff organisations opposed the outcome. The original negotiation results included permanent reductions in staff equivalent to a total of 212 full-time equivalents, 43 of which would take the form of redundancies. Uber, a United States transport technology company, dismissed more than 150 employees at its Kraków business services centre through a collective redundancy procedure completed at the end of July 2026. The company attributes the cuts to simplifying its organisational structure, merging teams and reducing costs, as part of a global reduction of around 3,300 posts. Staff serving notice were asked to train replacements brought to Kraków from India, and were offered financial incentives to take part. The e-commerce and logistics company Amazon has announced that it will transfer its air cargo operations from Malpensa Airport to Montichiari Airport in Lombardy. This change is expected to generate around 200 job opportunities in the Brescia area, although it will also impact approximately 190 individuals who are currently employed under the Amazon cargo contract at Malpensa. The transfer is due to begin on 8 September 2026, when it is expected to boost cargo activity at Montichiari. The affected workers are employed by handling and logistics service providers operating on the Amazon contract, rather than by Amazon directly. While trade unions welcomed the companies' willingness to explore redeployment solutions, they called for concrete commitments and a detailed implementation plan. On 3 September 2026, Regione Lombardia convened a meeting with the parties involved and requested operational proposals before the follow-up meeting scheduled for 24 September 2026. ELVO – Hellenic Vehicle Industries (2020), a Greek defence manufacturer, announced the creation of approximately 300 new jobs at its industrial complex in Sindos, Thessaloniki, as part of a €40 million business expansion. The new positions will mainly concern specialised engineers, technicians and production and operational staff. The investment will modernise and increase ELVO's existing military vehicle production capacity while establishing capabilities in additional defence systems and technologies, including unmanned aerial systems (UAS) and drones. Recruitment for the new positions has already begun and implementation of the investment is underway in phases. The programme builds on more than €20 million already invested by owner SK Group in restructuring the company, upgrading its facilities and improving production processes. Volkswagen Group, a German automotive giant, announced a global workforce adjustment of about 50,000 positions, about half of which will be cut in Germany. The reductions are targeted at indirect areas including management levels, where Volkswagen plans to cut around a quarter of management positions worldwide – from about 21,500 to 16,000. The restructuring is part of the company's Future Plan 2030, aimed at reducing complexity, tightening costs, accelerating digital innovation and expanding future mobility platforms. With the operating margin at 3.8% in the first half of 2026 against a 9% target for 2030, Volkswagen aims to cut overhead costs by €11 billion – roughly half of which are personnel costs, from which the figure of around 50,000 positions is derived. Production capacity is being reduced by a further 500,000 units per year in both Europe and China, while capital expenditure and R&D are budgeted at €135 billion for 2027-2031, around 25% below previous planning. Volkswagen's supervisory board approved the plan on 3 September 2026, two months after an earlier version had failed against opposition from employee representatives and the state of Lower Saxony. IG Metall and the Group Works Council said the agreement had prevented an escalation of the dispute, that a spin-off of the core VW passenger cars brand and components division was off the table, and that no plant had been given up – while stressing that management must now deliver on its responsibilities. The existing employment protection at Volkswagen AG and Volkswagen Sachsen, which rules out compulsory redundancies until the end of 2030, remains in force, and the detailed allocation of the cuts across brands and companies has yet to be negotiated with works councils. Volkswagen also announced that for the four plants in Emden, Zwickau, Hannover and Neckarsulm, current planning cannot guarantee competitive follow-up production from 2031 to 2034, and that alternative uses for the sites are being examined. A concept for a sustainable and competitive European production structure is due by the end of June 2027. In 2025, Volkswagen employed around 663,000 people worldwide, including approximately 284,000 in Germany. In December 2024, Volkswagen announced a restructuring programme which included the loss of 35,000 jobs in Germany. This event has been recorded in the ERM events database: Volkswagen 2024 - DE. Continental, a German automotive supplier, announced the closure of its solid-rubber industrial tyres production in Korbach, Hesse, which will affect about 140 employees by mid-2029 as production is shifted to Sri Lanka and Malaysia. The decision follows long-term underutilisation of capacity and increasing cost pressures. Continental aims to avoid dismissals and plans to implement socially responsible measures, such as career transition support and training for the 140 employees affected in Korbach. These measures are to be negotiated with the work council, which has criticizes Continental’s decision to close and outsource the production. The company employs around 2,400 people in Korbach. The remaining production activities at the site are not affected by the planned changes. ArcelorMittal, a multinational steel producer, announced the shutdown of its primary steel production facilities in Duisburg, resulting in approximately 550 job losses across the plant’s units. The closure is scheduled to conclude by October 2027. The planned restructuring would involve the closure of the steel plant, continuous casting facility and billet rolling mill, affecting around 550 jobs out of approximately 800 positions at the site. The company attributed the decision to the expiry of a long-term pig iron supply agreement with Thyssenkrupp Steel, unsuccessful attempts to secure alternative supplies, high CO₂ costs and challenging conditions in the European steel industry. Employee representatives are beginning social plan negotiations. The company employes 125,554 workers worldwide, among which 9,400 work at five sites in Germany. This restructuring follows previous restructuring events recorded in the ERM involving ArcelorMittal: ArcelorMittal Poland 2025 - PL, ArcelorMittal Services 2025 - FR, ArcelorMittal España 2024 - ES. Uber, an American transport technology company, announced a global restructuring that will eliminate roughly 3,300 positions, about 10 % of its worldwide workforce, bringing the total staff below 30,000. The cuts target managerial layers, small teams and technical, scientific and operations groups. The reshuffle aims to streamline governance, reduce layers, free capital for growth and innovation, especially in ride-hailing, delivery and autonomous mobility. Automation and AI already support customer service and other processes, driving the need for fewer staff. The first redundancies in Europe have already happened in Krakow - with 150 job cuts. Uber 2026 - PL The workforce reduction will occur across Uber’s global operations, the layoffs are planned to be completed shortly after the announcement, but an exact end date was not disclosed neither the exact locations of the layoffs. According to the management board, the restructuring aims to cut the company’s costs by 25%, also the use of new technologies, including AI, to streamline workflows as one of the reasons for the cuts. The trade union leader Cathrine Ertsås pointed a difficutl situation for Posten Bring, that have to face a strong competition and weak profitability, in this sense 250 jobs were already cut in 2025. Posten Bring 2024 - NO The Norwegian group employees around 12,649 staff. Cheminova, a Danish pesticide manufacturer owned by US group FMC and operating as FMC Rønland, announced on 1 September 2026 the closure of its plant at Rønland, Lemvig municipality, Western Jutland. Around 385 employees will be dismissed, with the site ceasing operation at the end of 2026. FMC links the decision to optimising its global production, following losses of about DKK 3 billion over three years and longstanding environmental problems as the company was producing pesticides not allowed in the EU and was exporting them to developing countries. All 385 losses are direct dismissals; affected staff were offered crisis-psychologist support. FMC has entered consultations with the local works council. Employment Minister Ane Halsboe-Jørgensen indicated that support running into millions of kroner could be available if Lemvig municipality applies to the national early-warning fund. Mayor Jens Lønberg Pedersen requested government help to create new jobs. The plant is Lemvig's largest workplace, and the site will not continue operating. Citation Eurofound (2026), Cheminova, Closure in Denmark, factsheet number 300940, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/300940. Vodafone Intelligent Solutions, a British-owned telecommunications and IT services provider operating in Spain and belonging to the Vodafone Group, has announced a 20% reduction of its Spanish workforce, equating to about 180 employees. The cuts will affect the division’s staff across all its Spanish locations, with no specific city singled out for the layoffs. The restructuring is expected to begin shortly after the announcement.Vodafone Intelligent Solutions has undertaken the job cut as part of an internal cost-optimisation strategy. The trade union UGT has challenged the necessity of the cuts, calling them "unnecessary and difficult to justify." Negotiations are ongoing, with unions seeking to reduce the number of affected workers or improve compensation. Sibanye Stillwater, a South African nickel refining company, has announced the closure of its Sandouville plant near Le Havre in France, which will result in the redundancy of over 100 employees. The first wave of departures is scheduled for January as part of a collective redundancy plan. This follows concerns about the plant's viability and the absence of investors for the planned battery-recycling project, which could have revitalised operations at the site. The closure is driven by commercial challenges, including the lack of buyers for the site after a temporary halt in production, as well as broader industry uncertainty. Trade unions are actively involved in the case. CGT representative Nicolas Quitard and CFE-CGC representative Emmanuel Leprevost criticised the closure announcement and expressed concern over the loss of industrial expertise. Citation Eurofound (2026), Sibanye Stillwater, Closure in France, factsheet number 300970, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/300970. response.description: The Wellbeing Services County of North Ostrobothnia Pohde, a Finnish regional public authority responsible for health, social and rescue services, announced the dismissal of 302 employees to reduce personnel costs by approximately €25 million. Up to 511 employment relationships may end in total, with further reductions pursued through retirements and the expiry of fixed-term contracts. Furloughs and part-time arrangements were also possible. The cuts affect staff across the regional authority in North Ostrobothnia. They are driven by a funding gap, as projected budget growth of approximately 1.6% falls short of rising salary and service costs. Reductions are concentrated among managers, specialists, administrative staff and patient-care workers. Tehy, the trade union, criticised the decision. Its chief shop steward at Pohde argued that staff were already under severe pressure and that workloads would increase for those remaining. Tehy also stated that it was not satisfied with the cooperation-negotiation process. Citation Eurofound (2026), The Wellbeing Services County of North Ostrobothnia Pohde, Internal restructuring in Finland, factsheet number 301039, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/301039. Rheinmetall, a German defence manufacturer, announced an expansion at its Neuss plant that could create up to 1200 new jobs, increasing the workforce from around 300 to 15000 employees. Rheinmetall will host approximately 500 scientists in an AI centre to be established on site, focusing on future technologies for security and satellite technology. Another 700 jobs will be created in the plant's production division. This development includes transforming the existing production site into a high-tech hub for radar satellites, drones and missile defence systems, alongside a new AI technology centre on an adjacent harbour area.The expansion is driven by the company’s ambition to strengthen its digital capabilities and meet the growing demand for advanced weapons technologies. The initiative underscores a broader move toward digitised defence solutions within Germany. The expansion reflects Rheinmetall’s strategy to maintain a leading position in Europe’s defence sector while investing heavily in high-tech research and development. On 27 August 2026, Rheinmetall announced the creation of 1,000 new jobs in Germany: Rheinmetall 2026 - DE. Baiersbronn Frischfaser Karton GmbH, a German packaging manufacturer specialising in corrugated cartons for the food, pharmaceutical and cosmetics sectors, announced the permanent closure of its plant in Baiersbronn, resulting in 220 job cuts. All employees will be dismissed by 07/09/2026 after the company completes remaining orders. The shutdown follows insolvency proceedings triggered by high production and energy costs, combined with a sharp decline in orders, and an unsuccessful search for new investment. The layoffs affect only the Baiersbronn site; all dismissals are direct due to plant closure. The firm reported €80 million revenue last year and had 220 staff at the time of announcement. The Prague Zoo, an organisation run by the city of Prague, has announced that it will expand its staff by 39 positions by January next year, focusing on positions in the field of animal care. The first wave of recruitment will begin on September 1st with the aim of acquiring 24 new employees, and the second wave will begin in January 2027 and will bring in 15 more employees. The expansion aims to improve staffing conditions, which were highlighted by a previous investigation that revealed staff shortages, overwork and low wages. By increasing the number of employees, the zoo wants to better distribute the workload, reduce reliance on overtime and improve the overall working atmosphere. All new hires will be based in Prague, and the total number of employees will increase from 250 to 289.
