AVL List, an Austrian automotive engineering company, announced the elimination of around 180 jobs in its Graz facility, reducing the number of employees to below 3,000. The layoffs are driven by weak market demand and postponed investment decisions from German and European customers, prompting the company to align its cost base with the current environment. The cuts target engineering, measurement technology and administration departments. All terminations involve amicable agreements across multiple departments. The job cuts represent the second wave of a two-wave restructuring that began in January, when a reduction of approximately 350 positions was announced AVL List - AT and a further totalled reduction of 450 jobs in 2025 AVL List - AT, AVL List - AT. Brovedani, an Italian manufacturer of automotive mechanical components, has announced the closure of its production plant in Modugno, Apulia. This will affect 44 employees. The production at the site would not resume after 7 September 2026 due to a reduction in business activity, and that manufacturing operations would be consolidated at its San Vito al Tagliamento facility in Friuli Venezia Giulia. The decision was also linked to rising raw material and energy costs, increased international competition, and the challenges currently facing the European automotive industry during its ongoing transition. The 44 employees are currently covered by a solidarity agreement until the end of September 2026. Discussions are ongoing regarding possible social protection measures and solutions to ensure employment continuity, including potential industrial conversion or reindustrialisation projects for the site. Trade unions FIM-CISL and FIOM-CGIL called for measures to safeguard employment, while the Apulia regional government convened a task force involving the company and employee representatives. Regional authorities have requested a technical review of available support instruments and participated in discussions with the Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy (MIMIT) to identify solutions for the affected workers and the future use of the site. Citation Eurofound (2026), Brovedani, Closure in Italy, factsheet number 300959, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/300959. Cuts will be implemented through collective redundancies. PayPal’s Irish workforce totals around 1,400 employees. Meanwhile the company announced 100 new jobs in Ireland in 2025 Paypal 2025 - IE. Cersanit S.A., a Polish ceramic manufacturer headquartered in Kielce, announced the dismissal of 487 employees across its production plants. The cuts will affect factories located in Krasnystaw, Starachowice, Opoczno, Radom and Wałbrzych, spreading from August to November 2026. The decision follows sharply rising energy and raw-material costs, disruptions caused by the Ukraine war and a sustained drop in demand for ceramics. Consequently, management has chosen to reduce staffing levels and concentrate production on its most efficient machine park. Cersanit currently employs about 5,500 people. Żarówka, a Polish manufacturing firm located in Pabianice, announced the closure of its century-old plant, resulting in 474 job losses. The factory’s operations will cease by the end of December, with layoffs commencing in September and finalizing at the end of the year. The decision follows failed attempts to secure an investor and the lack of financial viability for the facility, leading management to opt for permanent shutdown rather than restructuring or relocation. All 474 employees are affected within Pabianice, receiving a three-month notice period that constitutes direct dismissals. Picnic, a Dutch e-grocery company, has announced the creation of over 200 new jobs in France. These will include 40 delivery drivers and 40 order-preparation staff at its logistics hubs in Moissy, Cramayel and Fretin in the Hauts-de-France region. Additional managerial roles will support future warehouse openings in Ile-de-France. This expansion forms part of Picnic’s strategy to reinforce its teams at the two order-processing centres and 17 delivery hubs in order to meet growing demand and improve customer service by working with dedicated delivery partners. Picnic currently employs around 1,800 people across its operations. Several large-scale restructurings have been recorded in the ERM database, with the latest in Germany in 2025 Picnic 2025 - DE. GXO Logistics, a US-based contract logistics company, plans to create around 150 jobs at a new distribution centre at 7R Park Lavičky, near Velké Meziříčí. Recruitment was under way in August 2026, and operations are expected to reach full capacity in the second half of 2027. The expansion follows a multi-year agreement under which GXO will provide logistics services for L’Oréal across Central Europe. The facility is being developed by 7R with WOOD Real Estate as investment partner. The positions will be created gradually as the centre is prepared and brought into operation. The mayor of Velké Meziříčí raised concerns about additional lorry traffic associated with the development. Rheinmetall, a German defence manufacturer, has announced the creation of around 1,000 new jobs in Kassel and Calden through the construction of its Defence Hub Nordhessen, scheduled to begin operations in 2027. Supported by a €285 million investment from the state of Hesse, Rheinmetall plans to expand its plant in Kassel, build a new logistics and training centre, and establish drone testing facilities at the nearby Kassel-Calden Airport. With around 30,000 square metres, the logistics centre will be one of the company’s most significant infrastructure investments in Germany and an important part of Rheinmetall’s growth strategy in the field of tactical military vehicles. The new jobs will be created across Kassel and Calden and will cover a broad range of qualifications, including the construction, logistics and warehouse specialists as well as technical and administrative positions. Around 130 of these jobs will be located directly at the airport. Rheinmetall already employs around 2,200 people in Kassel. Appel Médical, a subsidiary of Randstad France, will create around 800 permanent positions in the medical and paramedical sectors. They will be recruiting professionals such as nurses, midwives, physiotherapists, doctors, pharmacists and support staff. This recruitment drive addresses the persistent difficulties in filling vacancies in the healthcare sector and aims to alleviate shortages of nursing staff and staff in certain medical specialities nationwide. In total, the recruitment agency has announced the creation of 5,220 jobs in total, considering temporary positions. The posts are spread across all French regions, with the highest numbers in Nouvelle-Aquitaine (900) and Occitanie (800). The remaining posts are distributed across the PACA region and Corsica (570 in total), Île-de-France (550), Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes (500), Brittany (460), Grand Est (440) and Pays de la Loire (400). Hauts-de-France and Bourgogne-Franche-Comté each have 300 posts, compared with 280 in Normandy. Previously, Appel Médical was mentioned in the ERM database for a recruitment of 300 new positions. R-Pharm, a German pharmaceutical manufacturer, announced the closure of its production facility in Illertissen, resulting in the loss of 280 jobs. The employment impact will be realised by the end of August 2026. The closure follows insolvency proceedings that were triggered by EU sanctions against Russia, which placed significant strain on the company's financial position. During the insolvency process, no investor could be found to secure the future of the site. The works council negotiated a social plan with the insolvency administrator, which provides for severance payments. However, given the company's difficult financial situation, it remains uncertain to what extent, and when, employees will actually receive these payments. The employees have received their notice of dismissal. However, around 50 to 60 employees will remain on fixed-term contracts to manage the winding-down of the site. Since 2014, the plant has been part of R-Pharm. Citation Eurofound (2026), R-Pharm , Bankruptcy in Germany, factsheet number 300927, European Restructuring Monitor. Wolfram Europa, an Estonian defence-technology company, plans to invest up to €200 million in a new explosives and warhead-production complex in Jēkabpils Municipality, Latvia. The project is expected to create approximately 200 highly skilled jobs, strengthen Latvia’s defence-industrial capacity and improve the security of regional supply chains. The facility will be developed in three phases on an approximately 40-hectare site south of Jēkabpils, although its precise location has not been disclosed for security reasons. Initial investment is estimated at around €50 million, with first-stage production expected to begin in the second half of 2027. Once fully operational, the vertically integrated complex will manufacture RDX, HMX and PBX explosives and assemble products such as warheads and anti-tank mines. Eberle, a precision engineering and industrial manufacturing company headquartered in Augsburg's Pfersee district, has announced that approximately 160 positions will be made redundant. The redundancies are the result of insolvency proceedings initiated due to liquidity constraints, which were exacerbated by high energy costs and geopolitical tensions, forcing the company to realign its cost structure. According to IG Metall, around 75 employees could be retained by a prospective buyer at a new site in the southern Augsburg district. Negotiations on a social compensation plan have been concluded, and the trade union IG Metall intends to support affected employees in their professional reorientation and transition to new employment opportunities. The company employs around 250 people, meaning that the announced redundancies will affect more than half of its workforce. As of September 2026, it is unknown when the job losses will be implemented. Updated, 16/09/2026 As of 4 September 2026, a local investor, Wikus Sägenfabrik, based out of Spangenberg, acquired Eberle's saw sales and bimetal divisions, retaining 74 employees at the Augsburg site. The remaining workforce from the other divisions is dismissed. This affects 160 employees. All job losses occur in the Augsburg Area. The IG Metall is actively supporting affected workers through training and job-placement efforts. EMA-LION Bonyhádi Zománcáru Kft., a Hungarian porcelain manufacturer, has announced the liquidation of its historic Bonyhád plant, bringing an end to operations at Hungary’s last traditional enameled cookware factory. The company will lay off its entire workforce, comprising roughly 150 employees. Liquidation proceedings began a couple of days before the announcement on 26 August 2026 and are expected to conclude once the liquidator terminates all employment contracts. The shutdown follows years of financial distress that left many workers unpaid. It will be the task of the liquidator, to be appointed by the commercial court, to settle outstanding wages, benefits payable during the notice period and severance pay. The Vasas Trade Union Federation has confirmed the news and is working to ensure that all employees depart under the best possible terms. The Bonyhád mayor offers mediation between the affected workers and employers in the region. According to the mayor, the region is experiencing a labour shortage, so those made redundant may be able to find new jobs in a relatively short time. RTP, the Portuguese public broadcaster, has announced a voluntary exit plan that will see 157 employees leave the organisation in 2026. The reduction is part of an internal restructuring aimed at ensuring financial sustainability and operational efficiency, with the workforce expected to drop from 1 764 staff in 2025 to 1 667 by the end of 2026. The plan operates under a 4:1 replacement ratio, requiring four departures for every new hire, and is projected to be fully implemented by October 2026. No outsourcing, offshoring or relocation measures are involved. The restructuring focuses on cost rationalisation across all units within Portugal and does not involve external social partners or specific regional sites; it represents a focused effort to streamline operations while maintaining RTP’s public service mandate. Halberstädter Konserven, a German meat-processing company, has announced the permanent closure of its production facility in Halberstadt. As a result, all 152 positions at the plant will be eliminated. Production will cease as the business is wound down. The trade union Nahrung-Genuss-Gaststätten (NGG) confirmed that all staff received dismissals. Employees are currently awaiting outstanding wages, as insolvency benefits have not yet been approved. The closure follows the company's third insolvency proceeding, which began in early June. The insolvency was driven by rising energy and raw material costs, as well as the generally challenging economic environment. The job losses are being implemented through direct redundancies. However, a number of the 152 employees have already left the company and secured new employment elsewhere. The business was founded more than 140 years ago. Amazon, a global e-commerce and technology company, is expanding its logistics operations in the industrial area of Rheinberg. The company is set to create 1,000 new jobs over the next two years, with construction and modernisation work already underway at the existing fulfilment centre. The expansion is focused on the integration of mobile robotic shelving units, automated conveyor systems and a new upper floor, increasing storage capacity to 20 million items, which is more than double the current volume. This will enable the site to dispatch up to 600,000 parcels per week, compared with around 140,000 at present. The growth forms part of Amazon’s commitment to the digital transformation of its European logistics network. By automating picking processes and reducing the distances employees need to travel within the warehouse, the company aims to improve operational efficiency while also creating new opportunities for staff training at nearby facilities, including the site in Mönchengladbach. The Rheinberg facility currently employs approximately 1,000 people. With the planned recruitment of a further 1,000 employees, the workforce is expected to double within the next two years. Nordic Sugar, a Danish sugar producer owned by the German group Nordzucker, announced on 25 August 2026 that it will end sugar production at its Nakskov plant on Lolland, resulting in the loss of 150 permanent positions among its 200 employees. Production will cease after the current harvest in January 2027, after which the site will be repurposed as a sugar packing facility. The company links the decision to strengthening the group's competitiveness and building a more efficient production network. Danish production will be concentrated at the Nykøbing plant on Falster. Nordic Sugar will support affected employees in moving to other work and consult employee representatives and Lolland Municipality on possible solutions. Danske Sukkerroedyrkere, the sugar-beet growers' association, reacted critically, with chairman Troels Frandsen calling for close dialogue with the company. Updated, 16/09/2026 Nordzucker has revised the employment impact of the Nakskov closure. Of the up to 150 jobs originally reported as affected, 70 employees will be made redundant (direct dismissals), 30 are offered alternative positions within the group, and 50 jobs are retained in the packaging department, which the facility will be converted into once sugar production ends after the current harvest in January 2027. OBOS, a Norwegian housing association in the real estate sector, announced the reduction of approximately 200 positions by the end of 2027. The cuts target staff and support functions across all divisions, including marketing, communications and IT roles. The restructuring is part of a corporate improvement programme aimed at cutting costs and boosting profitability, with an expected savings of about one billion kroner. It follows as a result of high interest rates and a downturn in the Norwegian housing market. The restructuring process is currently in its early stages, which include talks between trade unions and the management. Trade union representatives in HK, which organises around 200 employees in the company, describe the process so far as "orderly", and report that they are prioritizing seniority and social considerations in the process. DEMO, a Greek pharmaceutical manufacturer, is creating at least 600 direct jobs at its new pharmaceutical production campus in the Tripoli Industrial Area, Arcadia, Peloponnese. The new industrial complex will comprise four units for the production of pharmaceutical active ingredients and four units for finished pharmaceutical products, including penicillin and oncology medicines. The Tripoli development forms part of DEMO's wider €356 million investment programme, which is scheduled for completion by 2027 and aims to increase pharmaceutical production capacity and strengthen security of supply in Greece and the EU. In April 2026, the Greek Prime Minister visited the facilities while the investment was under implementation. Recruitment for the new Tripoli plant is currently underway, with DEMO advertising full-time, on-site positions for the facility. Recent reporting refers to more than 1,000 jobs associated with the investment; the factsheet uses the more conservative company-supported figure of at least 600 direct jobs. Security Services KUO, a Spanish private-security firm, has announced the collective dismissal of 163 staff as part of its liquidation proceedings in Spain. The company, which employs around 1,300 workers nationwide, is facing insolvency after months of unpaid wages and contract disputes. The dismissals are being carried out under the administration concursal’s Employment Regulation File (ERE), affecting personnel distributed across several provinces. Trade union FTSP-USO have warned about the impact on workers’ families and called for public authorities to ensure proper subrogation. In this regard, and under the current subrogation process, most of the remaining employees are transferred to the security companies taking over KUO’s contracts, allowing them to retain their jobs despite KUO’s closure. LUO S.r.l., an Italian business process outsourcing (BPO) and customer care company formed from the merger of Network Contacts and Step, announced a restructuring process involving 380 declared redundancies within its national workforce of over 3,000 employees. The measures stem from a framework agreement signed on 27 July 2026 between company management and national trade unions SLC-CGIL, FISTEL-CISL, UIL-FPC and UGL-Telecomunicazioni. The agreement introduces a nine-month defensive solidarity scheme, effective from 31 August 2026, covering roughly 1,093 employees across several sites, with working-time and pay cuts of up to 35%. It also provides for up to 150 voluntary redundancies nationally, to be carried out "exclusively on a voluntary, non-opposed basis," each compensated with one month's salary, alongside new smart-working rules capping in-office presence at 70% for operational staff and additional protections for vulnerable workers. The regional union CONF.I.A.L. Calabria, through regional secretary Fabio Tomaino, sharply criticised the agreement's inclusion of LUO's Crotone site, where around 200 jobs are considered at risk. The union said the process was conducted without a clear internal discussion of redundancies, that no local Crotone representatives were named in the agreement, and that conflicting signals exist: national union documents list Crotone among the sites under the solidarity scheme, while informal messaging has suggested otherwise. Tomaino demanded that any claimed crisis at the Crotone site be substantiated with documented data, financial statements and production/order volumes, arguing that available figures on declining volumes appear to concern other sites, such as Molfetta and Taranto, rather than Crotone. The union also disputed the company's framing of the reorganisation as "modern and sustainable," noting that promised AI-related reskilling programmes remain undefined. Homanit Lietuva, a Lithuanian subsidiary of German group Homann Holzwerkstoffe, operates in the wood products manufacturing sector. The company announced the temporary suspension of its timber board production line in Pagiriai, Vilnius region, leading to 200 job cuts across its workforce. The shutdown is effective immediately and will resume once market conditions stabilize. The decision follows weaker than expected first-half results driven by a global decline in furniture demand and heightened costs for energy, wood, chemicals, and transport linked to the Middle East conflict. Homanit Lietuva aims to reduce losses of €5–6 million before resuming full operations. All 200 contract terminations are direct dismissals at the Pagiriai plant. During the interim, approximately 20 employees will remain on site to maintain essential functions. The company currently employs about 255 people across its facilities. Universitätsklinikum Frankfurt, a German public hospital, is planning to cut up to 500 jobs. The planned reductions are expected to affect primarily administrative roles. The restructuring programme, which has been overseen by an external consultancy since February 2026, is intended to address persistent financial deficits that reached approximately €21 million last year. The initiative forms part of broader efforts to restore the hospital's financial stability following a prolonged period of losses. While the hospital has confirmed that job cuts will take place, it has not yet confirmed the exact number of positions affected or how the measures will be implemented. Several employees have, however, reported that up to 500 jobs could be at risk. Universitätsklinikum Frankfurt employs around 8,500 people. Recruitment will take place nationwide, including at the company’s depots in Dublin, Galway and Cork. response.description: The office of the Government of the Czech Republic (Úřad vlády ČR), a central government body responsible for tasks relating to the professional, organisational and technical support of the activities of the Czech Government and its bodies, announced that it will cut 243 positions in Prague, reducing its workforce from 643 to roughly 400 employees by the end of the year. The announced reduction of approximately 243 positions at the Government Office does not equate to the same number of job losses, as a portion of the workforce is being reallocated to ministries. In particular, 22 positions have been transferred to the Ministry of Justice, 10 to the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, and additional positions to the Ministry of Health. This measure is being implemented primarily with the aim of reducing the Office’s budget to 820 million CZK in 2026. Engmatec, a German machine engineering company, has announced that it will cease operations, resulting in the closure of its production site in Radolfzell am Bodensee. The company's 150 employees, specialised in the field of automation and testing technology, have already received notice of termination, and the winding-up process is expected to be completed by October. The closure follows insolvency proceedings under self-administration, which were initiated in spring 2026 but ultimately failed to attract the investment needed to secure the company's future. The insolvency was triggered by a weak economic environment, declining order volumes, international price competition and rising costs. A social plan has been agreed with the works council to support affected employees in finding new employment opportunities. Founded in 1994, the company is now focusing on completing its remaining customer orders before operations are fully discontinued. Lear, an automotive parts supplier, has announced the closure of its plant in Gründau, resulting in the loss of approximately 180 jobs across production and logistics functions. The redundancy process is now under way, and the site is scheduled to cease operations by mid-2027. As part of a global realignment strategy, Lear intends to discontinue its production and logistics activities at the Gründau facility and transfer the remaining production capacity to Slovakia, Serbia and Tunisia. The company will, however, retain around 120 engineering positions at the site. Representatives of the works council and the IG Metall trade union have strongly opposed the decision, highlighting the legal protections afforded to employees under the applicable collective agreement. Negotiations on a social plan are expected to begin in the coming weeks in order to support affected employees. Lear currently employs around 300 people at the Gründau site. New outlets are planned for Madrid’s Príncipe Pio shopping centre, Valladolid, La Línea de la Concepción and Bilbao. These openings aim to strengthen JD Sports’ presence in key urban markets by offering larger, more innovative retail spaces that cater to evolving consumer habits. The job creation will be concentrated mainly in Madrid and Barcelona, with additional roles spread across the other new locations. JD Sports currently employs over 3 100 staff in Spain and intends to reach a total of 138 points of sale by early 2027, further consolidating its retail footprint throughout the country. Espersen, a Danish fish-processing company, is restructuring its operations in Koszalin. The company plans to close and sell its primary processing facility in the city, affecting around 650-700 production workers. The consultation process began in mid-2026, with the first 227 employees receiving dismissal notices by the end of August, effective from November 2026. Further reductions may follow depending on the outcome of the sale process. Espersen will continue production at its second Koszalin site. According to the company, the decision reflects long-term changes in the whitefish processing market. Espersen cited reduced cod and haddock quotas. The affected workforce consists mainly of production employees. Espersen has indicated that a transfer of ownership would be preferable, as it could preserve part of the existing employment base. The Koszalin District Labour Office (PUP) has been supporting affected workers and monitoring the collective redundancy process. Local authorities, including the Mayor of Koszalin, have pledged support in identifying potential investors. Espersen is one of Europe's largest fish processors. The company operates facilities in Poland, Denmark, the United Kingdom and Vietnam. In Koszalin, it has historically been one of the region's largest employers, with total employment fluctuating between 1,300 and 2,000 workers. St Bernhard Hospital in Brake, a German healthcare institution, has announced the closure of its facility, resulting in the loss of approximately 350 jobs at the site in August 2026. The closure follows insolvency proceedings initiated last year. Although the hospital had originally been expected to cease operations in September, the shutdown has been brought forward to August as patient numbers and staffing levels have continued to decline and the financial crisis has worsened. There have been disputes between the workforce and the hospital management over a social plan. No concrete social plan has been agreed. In addition, the insolvency wage scheme secures the salaries of the approximately 350 employees only until 14 August 2026. A review of potential claims for damages has been initiated. Accell Hunland Kft., a Hungarian subsidiary of Dutch bicycle manufacturer Accell Group, started the insolvency proceedings and announced the closure of its Tószeg plant, resulting in 400 job losses. The layoffs will begin after the notice issued on Thursday. The decision follows prolonged financial strain and a post-pandemic drop in demand for bicycles, following a temporary demand surge during the COVID pandemic. Accell Group was acquired by the US investment firm KKR (Kohlberg Kravis Roberts) in 2022. The industry downturn began in the following year and eventually culminated in the bankruptcy of the company. The closure of the Tószeg plant creates significant problems not only for the small town but also for the nearby county seat, Szolnok, as well, since Accell was both the largest local employer and the largest local taxpayer. The mayor of Szolnok called on the leading companies in the city to hire, where possible, some of the laid-off employees, and took on the role of coordinator between the workers and potential new employers. Estonian municipal kindergartens, operating across the country’s education sector, announced the dismissal of several hundred staff members due to new language proficiency requirements. The workforce affected includes kindergarten teaching assistants in Tallinn and Narva, reflecting a national policy shift aimed at ensuring all early-childhood educators meet B2 language level by 1 August 2026. The restructuring is driven by regulatory compliance. The mandate for higher language skills has forced municipalities to lay off employees that do not meet the criteria, while simultaneously recruiting new ones, which has led to hiring people who possess the required linguistic ability but lack formal teaching qualifications. Even though exact statistics are not yet available, according to the deputy mayor, there are around 100 vacancies still unfilled in Tallinn. In response to skill gaps, local authorities are partnering with Tartu Health College to provide rapid training programmes, offering practical instruction for new hires and ongoing support for existing staff. The changes highlight a broader move toward improving early-childhood education quality in Estonian. Schaeffler, a German industrial and automotive supplier, has announced the reduction of approximately 1,300 positions across its German operations. The workforce reduction is scheduled to begin this year, although no specific completion date has been announced. The measure is intended to reduce costs and improve the company’s competitiveness in response to challenging market conditions and stagnant sales. The job cuts will be implemented through partial retirement schemes (Altersteilzeit) aimed at employees born in or before 1971. Under these arrangements, employees work reduced hours and receive adjusted pay for a period of between two and eight years, followed by a phase during which they continue to receive compensation while no longer actively working. Participation is entirely voluntary and requires the agreement of both the employee and their respective line manager. The programme has been agreed with the works council. Schaeffler implemented a similar measure in 2024, which resulted in approximately 2,800 job cuts Schaeffler 2024 - DE. The company had also announced a workforce reduction of 74 positions in Ingolstadt in early 2026 Schaeffler 2026 - DE. Schaeffler employs around 110,000 people worldwide. response.description: The Center for the Transformation of Chemistry (CTC), a German research initiative in the chemical sector, is expected to create up to 1,000 jobs. The majority, around 700 positions, will be located at its main site in Delitzsch, with approximately 300 additional roles at the Merseburg site. Recruitment has already begun, with 70 employees currently working at the CTC, and the organisation is expected to reach its target workforce size by 2038. The Center for the Transformation of Chemistry (CTC) aims to drive the transformation of the chemical industry towards a sustainable circular economy. From 2027, the CTC plans to train its own specialists, with recruitment for chemistry laboratory technician apprenticeships expected to begin in late 2026. Further training programmes in IT and office administration may follow at a later stage. Current employees work across scientific and administrative functions. Citation Eurofound (2026), Center for the Transformation of Chemistry, Business expansion in Germany, factsheet number 300834, European Restructuring Monitor. All 150 positions are concentrated at the Swarożynie facility, with recruitment currently underway and anticipated start of employment in the coming months. Department of Education Narva, an Estonian public entity in the education sector, announced 108 job cuts affecting assistant teachers in kindergartens across Narva. The cuts involve contract terminations as of 3 August 2026. The restructuring follows new language proficiency requirements mandating a minimum B2 level in Estonian for all teaching assistants. The Ministry of Education assumes that there will be no disruption of child care provision, as remaining staff will fill vacancies and complete teams should be operational by 1st of September.The job losses are concentrated in the city of Narva and Tallinn, affecting only assistant teachers, no other roles are impacted. In Tallinn, not meeting the language requirements affected around 300 teaching assistants who have all been laid off, but already 90 new people have been hired. No additional dismissal mechanisms were reported, and all contracts were terminated directly.The restructuring is purely internal with no outsourcing or relocation plans. Social partners have not been mentioned in the announcement, and the change will be fully implemented by the announced date. IBIH Advanced Materials, a Chinese manufacturer of advanced battery materials, opened its first Slovak plant in Trnava. The factory is located in CTPark Trnava and aims to employ 100 to 120 people in total once fully operational, of which around 60 positions have already been filled. The expansion is driven by growing demand for electric-vehicle components and the company's investment of €10 million into the site, positioning it as a supplier of thermal-insulation and fire-protection pads for EV batteries in Europe. All new jobs are being created at the Trnava location. The plant currently employs around 60 workers, roughly half of the planned 100–120 total, with the remaining positions expected to be filled as production ramps up toward full capacity. About 50 positions have already been opened and an additional 50 are expected by year-end. Regiocom Bulgaria employs over 1,700 staff across eight Bulgarian cities and plans further hiring at its other sites throughout 2026. JTEKT Czech Republic, a Japanese-owned automotive component manufacturer based in Plzen, Czechia, announced the elimination of roughly 300 positions. The reduction represents almost half its workforce from its production plant and associated support roles. The decision is part of a strategic reshaping aimed at stabilising the branch and aligning capacity with market dynamics. The plant will remain operational with a reduced workforce. The Employment Office is in contact with the company and has offered to provide assistance. Dismissals are scheduled to begin at the end of August 2026, with reductions expected within that month. All affected employees will receive severance pay, and production remains ongoing in Czechia. The site employed 620 staff before the cuts, and its parent Jtekt Corporation continues unchanged operations elsewhere. The program offers generous incentives, including enhanced severance, extended pre-retirement plans and relocation support. Trade unions CC. OO. and UGT have urged the company to preserve the voluntary nature of exits and safeguard generational succession plans. Carrefour Services Clients, the French customer-service of the Carrefour distribution group, announced the closure of its call centre in Saint-Étienne, which will result of one hundred job cuts. The unit has been operated since 1999 and is scheduled to shut down at the end of December. Several employees have been offered internal reclassifications. At the headquarters in Évry-Courcouronnes, ten internal reclassifications are also in progress. The management justifies the restructuring by a structural decline in customer complaints and an increased demand for immediate responses. The trade union, FO, criticised the outsourcing strategy as means to reduce costs and protested the decision. Social partners and employee representatives are currently negotiating with management, through the works council. They mandated a consulting firm to handle negotiations. Several large-scale restructurings have been recorded in ERM, with the latest recorded in Poland in 2026 Carrefour Polska 2026 - PL. Gibert Joseph, a French bookseller, announced 84 job cuts as part of its transformation plan. The cuts affect its physical stores, notably the historic boutique on Boulevard Barbès in Paris. The restructuring is driven by an ongoing decline in the new-book market and the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic that have pressured sales and profitability. The company has struggled to invest in its online platform, reducing its competitiveness and contributing to the decision to close several outlets. All job losses are concentrated in Paris. Social partners are represented by the CGT union, with delegates Noémie Hardy and Rémy Frey voicing concerns and protests about the plan. Gibert Joseph employs approximately 500 staff, so the 84 cuts represent roughly one-seventh of its workforce. Amazon, a US-based online retail and logistics company, has announced an expansion of its logistics centre in Pforzheim, Baden-Württemberg, Germany, which will create 1,000 new jobs by the end of 2029. The expansion centres on a new robotics-enabled logistics hub that will store around 20 million items and utilise hundreds of transport robots to move goods, reducing the distances employees need to travel and increasing productivity. Digital automation is the main driver behind the job creation, with Amazon positioning the facility as a leading high-tech logistics site. The mayor welcomed the investment of more than €300 million and the creation of new jobs, highlighting the positive impact on the regional economy. Job profiles include: specialists, management, and non-qualified warehouse and fulfillment staff. The latest internal restructuring measure at Amazon was recorded in the ERM database earlier in 2026, involving the creation of 420 jobs in Brandenburg Amazon 2026 - DE. The site currently employs around 1,000 people, meaning that the expansion will double the existing workforce. BMW, a German automotive manufacturer, has announced that approximately 8,000 jobs will be cut worldwide. Of the company's roughly 154,000 employees globally, around 84,000 are based in Germany. It has therefore been reported that at least half of the planned job reductions are expected to affect Germany, amounting to a minimum of around 4,000 positions. The job cuts are scheduled to begin in October 2026 and are expected to be completed by the end of 2027. The restructuring is being driven by weak market conditions in the automotive industry, growing competition from China and US tariffs. The company aims to improve its profitability and competitiveness. The reductions will primarily affect administrative, development, research, planning and management functions, while production roles are expected to remain unaffected. An agreement on the workforce reduction plan has been reached with the works council. The company intends to implement the reductions through a voluntary severance programme combined with natural attrition. In Germany, around 40,000 employees are expected to receive individual offers under the programme. A previous business expansion was recorded in the ERM database in June 2026, when BMW announced the creation of 1,600 new jobs in connection with the opening of a new plant in Irlbach-Straßkirchen BMW 2026 - DE. The closure follows a sustained decline in demand for printed magazines and catalogues, as publishers and industrial clients increasingly shift towards digital formats, prompting a strategic review within the Bertelsmann Group. The company is now seeking to negotiate a social plan with employee representatives. The workforce reduction is intended to be implemented in a socially responsible manner, with measures such as severance payments and the establishment of a transfer company currently under consideration. Concentrix, an American outsourcing firm, has announced the elimination of 154 jobs at its A Coruña customer-service center in Spain. The unit, which originally employed 387 staff, will see these positions terminated by the end of August 2026. The layoffs stem from Microsoft’s decision to close two support campaigns—CTS and SCIM—in the city. The cuts result from a strategic withdrawal by Microsoft and Concentrix’s reliance on that single client, which has rendered the center highly vulnerable. Although no new clients have been secured and there are no indications of relocation or offshoring, Concentrix has attempted to improve dismissal terms through collective agreements with unions. The first wave of 75 dismissals took effect on the 31st of July, while a second group of 79 staff will be dismissed later in the month. Collective negotiations have involved the trade-union groups CIG, CCOO and UGT, with CGT opting not to sign the agreement. Updated, 27/08/2026 The second ERE in Concentrix’s A Coruña centre dismissed 79 workers after a first wave of 75, bringing total layoffs to 154 by 31 August 2026. Negotiations with unions ended without agreement and the committee will challenge the ERE in court. The investment reflects the company's commitment to digitalisation and the green transition, incorporating advanced electronics as well as renewable energy technologies such as photovoltaic systems and geothermal heating to enable climate-neutral operations. It also highlights a growing demand for highly skilled technical staff, particularly train electricians and other high-tech maintenance specialists. Previous internal restructuring measures were recorded in the ERM database in early 2026, involving 100 job cuts in Paderborn Deutsche Bahn 2026 - DE, and in 2025, when 1,000 jobs were cut Deutsche Bahn 2025 - DE. Franz Schneider, a German toy manufacturer, has announced the closure of its production facility in Neustadt bei Coburg, resulting in the loss of more than 110 jobs, affecting the entire workforce, with operations scheduled to cease at the end of December 2026. The restructuring follows the company's insolvency, which was triggered by the loss of its second-largest customer in 2025, rising energy and raw material costs associated with the war in Ukraine, increasing competition from China, and the impact of US tariffs. During the insolvency proceedings, it was not possible to restructure the business successfully and preserve operations. All job losses will be compulsory redundancies. Employees who remain with the company until the closure date will receive a retention bonus. The shutdown marks the end of operations in Germany for the family-owned business, which was founded in 1938. response.description: Knorr-Bremse GmbH Division IFE Automatic Door Systems, a German company operating in the transportation systems sector, announced the reduction of 41 positions at its Kematen site in Austria. The cuts are part of the group’s strategy to enhance cost efficiency and competitiveness amid challenging market conditions. The restructuring focuses on streamlining operations within the doors business unit without affecting the global headquarters status in Kematen. All 41 job losses will take place at the Kematen facility, which currently employs about 371 staff. Discussions with affected employees will occur at the end of August and beginning of September, accompanied by a negotiated social plan to mitigate economic and social consequences. The works council has agreed on the social plan and is involved in consultations; however, criticism has occurred as despite a highly profitable EBIT margin of over 10%, job cuts are foreseen. Employees argue there is no economic emergency justifying the cuts, suspecting a systematic relocation of expertise and value creation to India, where capacities are currently expanding. Citation Eurofound (2026), Knorr-Bremse Division IFE Automatic Door Systems, Internal restructuring in Austria, factsheet number 300873, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/300873. Wonderplant, a Greek company active in hydroponic agricultural production, is creating 300 direct permanent jobs at a new hydroponic tomato greenhouse facility in Mavropigi, Eordaia, near Ptolemaida in Western Macedonia. Works on the approximately €130 million investment started on 23 July 2026. The new facility will cover around 300 stremmata and is designed to produce approximately 20,000 tonnes of fresh table tomatoes annually. It will also include a 30 MW high-efficiency combined heat and power unit. The investment is supported by €63 million from the Just Transition Fund and forms part of efforts to develop new productive activities on former lignite land in Western Macedonia. Gradual operation of the new facility is expected to begin in early 2027, with full development targeted by the end of 2027. Wonderplant currently employs 439 workers at its existing hydroponic greenhouse facility in Petrousa, Drama, which provides the model for the new Ptolemaida investment. Nitrochemie, a German defence and chemical company and a subsidiary of Rheinmetall, is building a new propellant powder plant in Aschau am Inn, Bavaria, which will create approximately 300 to 500 new jobs. Production at the new facilities is scheduled to begin in 2027, with the full employment impact and production capacity expected to be reached in 2028. The expansion reflects Germany’s commitment to strengthening domestic ammunition production and securing the European defence supply chain. The initiative underlines the strategic importance of advanced propellant manufacturing for national defence and helps to enhance resilience against potential supply disruptions. Through the investment, the company aims to more than double its annual production capacity for propellants used in artillery ammunition. BBS Automation, a German machinery and plant engineering company and a subsidiary of Dürr, has announced the reduction of around 500 positions worldwide, including approximately 200 jobs across four sites in Germany. The job cuts are scheduled to be completed in 2027. The company makes part of its business with production equipment for the automotive industry, especially for electric cars. In addition, the company offers, among other things, systems for the production of medical devices such as syringes. The downsizing programme forms part of an efficiency strategy aimed at achieving annual savings of around €30 million. The reduction is attributed to weak demand in the automotive sector and subdued investment activity. The company intends to enter into negotiations with employee representatives to determine how the job cuts will be implemented. In 2025, BBS Automation had already announced 500 job cuts worldwide Dürr - DE, around half of which were in Germany Dürr - DE. BBS Automation currently employs approximately 2,500 people worldwide. DEHN, a German manufacturer of electrical equiment, has inaugurated its first production unit in Romania. The new facility, located in Pitești within CTPark Pitești, is expected to create up to 150 jobs across production, logistics and support services. This expansion is part of DEHN’s strategy to meet growing demand in European markets, complementing its automated German plants with specialized manual assembly. The Romanian unit will produce surge-protection devices and reinforce the company’s global manufacturing network. By establishing this site, DEHN strengthens Romania’s position as a destination for advanced industrial investment and enhances regional connectivity through proximity to major transport routes. The company plans to invest around 10 million euros in this Eastern European plant over the coming years. The company cited strategic and economic reasons, including weak demand for high-priced adult products and recent losses. As Pinqponq employs around 300 people, the planned reduction represents approximately 10% of its workforce. Stadtverwaltung Dresden, the municipal authority of the City of Dresden, has announced plans to reduce its administrative workforce. An earlier internal plan from 2025 had envisaged the elimination of 875 full-time positions, but the more recent proposal foresees a larger reduction of at least 1,200 positions. The restructuring is due to commence this year and is expected to be completed by the end of 2031. The planned workforce reduction affects public sector employees and forms part of the city's efforts to lower personnel costs in response to growing financial pressures, with expenditure having exceeded revenue for several consecutive years. The specific measures through which the job cuts will be implemented have not been disclosed. The City of Dresden currently employs 7,375 people. Vishay Siliconex, a semiconductor manufacturer operating in Germany, has announced the creation of more than 100 new jobs at its production facility in Itzehoe. Initial project announcements in 2023 referred to the creation of 150 jobs, while more recent reporting in July 2026 states that more than 100 jobs are expected to be created. The expansion forms part of an investment programme worth more than €400 million and aims to double the production capacity for chip switches used in automotive power transistors. The initiative is linked to the European Union's Chips Act, which seeks to strengthen semiconductor manufacturing within Europe and reduce dependence on imports from Asia. By expanding its facility in Itzehoe, Vishay is supporting this strategic objective. Vishay employs more than 22,000 people worldwide. Zalando, a German online fashion retailer, has announced plans to cut around 200 jobs at its Berlin headquarters as part of an ongoing restructuring programme following its acquisition of About You. The restructuring is already underway in 2026. The measures are intended to streamline organisational structures and enable the company to respond more quickly to changes in the market. The workforce reduction in Berlin is to be implemented through mutually agreed termination agreements. Zalando also plans to relocate certain positions and processes to Bucharest, where it intends to open a new office by the end of 2026 and create 60 jobs by the first quarter of 2027. Zalando previously announced the elimination of 180 jobs in Berlin following the closure of its "Zalando Content Solutions division" Zalando 2026 - DE . The company had also reduced its workforce in Berlin by around 450 positions in the previous year Zalando 2025 - DE. Zalando is one of Europe's leading online fashion platforms and employs approximately 15,000 people worldwide. McDonald's France, the French subsidiary of the fast-food restaurant chain McDonald's, announced the creation of 1,600 permanent jobs per year in its restaurant network in France. The recruitment programme was formalised through a national roadmap signed on 20 July 2026 and will continue until 2030, with the plan to create 8,000 positions. The initiative targets individuals in need of work, those with disabilities and single-parent families, aiming to hire locally at its restaurants across France. McDonald’s emphasizes proximity recruiting to reduce commuting times and tailor contracts to each territory. Social partners have been engaged in the national roadmap aswell. France Travail and Cheops (Cap emploi) signed the agreement at a Puteaux restaurant, ensuring collaboration between the company and public employment services. Amaco, an Italian public transport operator, announced that 108 employees of its municipalised transport unit in Cosenza will be directly dismissed as part of its judicial liquidation. The company is set to cease operations after the provisional exercise concludes on 30 September 2026, with assets slated for auction from its headquarters at Contrada Torrevecchia. The closure follows failed attempts by Consorzio Autolinee to acquire Amaco and a €2.1 million offer that was rejected, leaving the municipal transport service in transition. Trade unions have opposed the employment losses and called for institutional intervention to safeguard jobs and ensure continuity of public transport services. Pyszne.pl, the Polish subsidiary of Dutch food delivery group Just Eat Takeaway, announced the termination of its current cooperation model with around 5,000 couriers across Poland. The restructuring affects the Scoober delivery unit and will be implemented between August and September 2026. The company cites high operating costs, the need to increase scalability, and competitive pressure as the main reasons for the restructuring. The change involves outsourcing delivery operations to external fleet partners. OPZZ Konfederacja Pracy, a polish trade union, criticised the restructuring, raising concerns about reduced income, security and working conditions, linking the restructuring to upcoming regulatory changes regarding platform work in Poland. Trade unions have also discussed the changes with management, while public bodies responsible for labour law PIP and ZUS have launched inspections related to employment practices. Affected couriers may apply to work for one of five external fleet partners, but employment is not guaranteed. The new model is expected to replace guaranteed hourly pay they had at Pyszne.pl. Thyssenkrupp Polysius, a German manufacturer of cement plant equipment, announced the reduction of 430 positions at its Beckum site. Changing requirements of industrial customers are the reason for the restructuring. The company is strengthening its focus on the longevity of the equipment it manufactures, its modernization, and the replacement of spare parts. The Company is shifting towards sustainable process technologies. The number of employees will fall below 200 following plans to implement reductions gradually over an extended period and use settlement agreements together with natural attrition. The IG Metall had first criticized the reduction. It called for a transparent process and solutions to safeguard jobs. Later, the company, the IG Metall and the works council engaged in negotiations that culminated in an interest-settlement plan, mitigating job losses for many employees. The reduction only applies to the site in Beckum and operational continuity is maintained in Beckum. This restructuring follows two reductions that culminated in the loss of 300 jobs at the Beckum site in 2024: Thyssenkrupp Polysius 2024 - DE. ROQ, a Portuguese textile technology company based in Vila Nova de Famalicão, has announced a collective redundancy process affecting around 11% of its workforce, leaving the company with approximately 400 employees. Based on the company's statement that it will retain around 400 employees, the restructuring is estimated to result in approximately 50 job cuts. ROQ plans to concentrate resources on strategic business areas while increasing investment in innovation, technological development and operational efficiency. The company stated that it will maintain operations across all the markets in which it operates and continue delivering ongoing projects and customer services. ROQ has more than 40 years of activity and exports its products to over 80 countries through its ROQ and ROQ Laser businesses. Magna, a Canadian automotive supplier, has announced the permanent closure of its production plant in Dorfprozelten, Bavaria, Germany. The shutdown will result in the loss of 216 jobs and is scheduled to take effect by mid-2027. The company cites the ongoing crisis in the automotive industry, adverse market conditions and negative business performance as the main reasons for ceasing operations at the site. Despite previous investments and cost-cutting measures, the facility was considered no longer viable, and no new product programmes have been allocated to the plant. Representatives of IG Metall expressed dissatisfaction over what they described as broken promises regarding the future of the facility, as in 2023 the company had assured the union that the site would remain operational until the end of 2028. Magna International employs approximately 154,000 people worldwide across 28 countries. Previous internal restructuring measures were recorded in the ERM database in 2025, resulting in the loss of 162 jobs Magna 2025 - DE. Kodi, a German discount retailer, announced the initiation of insolvency proceedings and a restructuring programme in July 2026, affecting its 150 stores nationwide and approximately 1,200 employees. The company plans to close around 50 stores and reduce its workforce across the chain. The decision has been driven by weak consumer confidence, increasing competition from digital retail models, high energy and rental costs, and rising labour expenses. Store closures will be implemented over the coming weeks. The remaining 100 outlets will continue operating under temporary insolvency administration, while affected employees will receive wage protection for the period from July to September 2026. The exact number of redundancies has not yet been announced; however, the planned store closures indicate significant job losses. Kodi had previously filed for insolvency at the end of 2024, which resulted in 520 job cuts Kodi 2025 - DE. Updated 09/09/2026) The company announced that 19 stores will close, all of them in North Rhine-Westphalia. The future of a further 56 stores remains uncertain, while 69 locations are expected to remain open. Aer Lingus, an Irish airline under the International Airlines Group, announced that 500 positions will be cut as part of a cost-cutting programme: 70 pilots, 140 cabin crew members and 290 head-office roles. The restructuring targets employees based in Ireland, with head-office roles concentrated at its Dublin headquarters.The cut includes a quarter of its management jobs: 20 general managers and senior staff have taken voluntary redundancy. Rising fuel costs, intensified North American competition and the need to meet IAG’s profitability targets prompted the move. In addition, the airline will reduce flights from Dublin to Denver, Minneapolis, Las Vegas and Split. The unions Fórsa, IALPA, and SIPTU, have expressed opposition to compulsory redundancies, warning that the cuts could impact workforce stability. Aer Lingus intends to complete the programme within the coming months as negotiations progress. Dumarey, a Tuscan automotive component manufacturer based in Fauglia and San Piero a Grado near Pisa, currently has 850 employees covered by solidarity contracts that run until the end of 2026. The restructuring is a response to Volkswagen factory closures and aims to preserve employment through extended solidarity agreements rather than immediate layoffs. Job losses are concentrated within the Fauglia and San Piero a Grado sites, while all 850 employees remain under protection until 31/12/2026. However the company mentioned they won't extend the protection to next year. Social partners involved include Fiom Cgil; they have advocated for contract extensions and engaged with regional authorities to safeguard employment in the sector. Updated, 21/07/2026 Despite an agreement signed in April 2026 between the company and the Tuscany Region concerning 93 staff leasing workers, it is expected that 35 of these employees will leave the company by the end of July 2026. The agreement stipulated that these workers were to remain in employment until 31 December 2026. A further 53 staff leasing workers may also be affected before the end of 2026. Salzgitter, a German steel manufacturer, has announced its takeover of HKM, the Duisburg steelworks, a move that will result in around 2,000 job cuts by the end of 2028. The restructuring is being driven by the transition towards green steel production. Salzgitter plans to invest in an electric arc furnace, which is expected to significantly reduce CO₂ emissions and help secure the long-term viability of the site. The company has emphasised that it would not have been able to proceed with the full acquisition without the planned workforce reduction. The job reductions are intended to be implemented in a socially responsible manner, although the company has not disclosed any specific measures. HKM most recently employed around 3,000 people. Following the restructuring, the workforce is expected to be reduced to approximately 1,000 employees. Prior to the transaction, Thyssenkrupp Steel Europe (TKSE) held a 50% stake in HKM, while Salzgitter and Vallourec owned 30% and 20% respectively. Updated, 20/07/2026 IG Metall negotiated a social collective agreement with the employer. Under the agreement, around 300 more jobs will be retained than originally planned. As a result, 1,700 jobs, rather than the initially announced 2,000, will be eliminated at the Duisburg site. The agreement also sets out the accompanying measures for the workforce reduction. It provides for a phased and predictable downsizing process over several years. For some employees, employment ended on 30 June 2026. The company is now seeking 500 volunteers who are willing to leave the company from 1 October 2026 onwards. Salzgitter plans to construct an electric arc furnace at the Duisburg site, which has been described as the largest of its kind in Germany. Citation Eurofound (2026), HKM, Merger/Acquisition in Germany, factsheet number 300730, European Restructuring Monitor. Dublin, https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/300730. O2 Telefónica Deutschland, the German subsidiary of the Spanish Telefónica Group operating in the telecommunications sector, has announced that more than 1,000 positions are expected to be eliminated, although no definitive completion date has yet been provided. The restructuring follows the loss of its largest customer, 1&1, and forms part of a broader transformation programme aimed at safeguarding the company's long-term competitiveness. It also reflects wider pressures within the telecommunications industry, where growth opportunities in the mobile market are limited, competition remains intense, and the returns on network investments have become increasingly difficult to realise. The workforce reductions are expected to be achieved primarily through voluntary departures and severance arrangements rather than compulsory redundancies. Management stated that it is currently discussing and assessing potential measures together with employee representatives. The company employs approximately 6,820 people. Updated, 22/07/2026 O2 Telefónica Deutschland has announced that the number of positions to be cut will amount to up to 1,100. The company has now also provided a timetable for the workforce reduction, which is due to be completed by the end of 2026 and includes the closure of 60 stores. The reduction will be achieved through voluntary departures and severance packages. A second round of job cuts is expected next year. Updated, 18/08/2026 According to information obtained by Handelsblatt, O2 Telefónica Germany is planning to cut up to 1,650 jobs by 2028. This represents a 50% increase on the 1,100 redundancies previously announced for implementation by the end of 2026. The company stated that the measures are intended to safeguard its competitiveness. Jelcz, a Polish manufacturer of military trucks belonging to Polska Grupa Zbrojeniowa, announced an expansion of production in Racibórz based on assets of the former Rafako plant. The investment is expected to create more than 500 jobs at the Racibórz site, where recruitment has already started. The project is linked to the planned merger of Jelcz with RFK, with Jelcz as the acquiring company. Pfizer, a multinational pharmaceutical company, has announced approximately 370 job cuts (330 direct employees and 40 agency workers) at its production plant in Catania, Italy. The restructuring follows a downsizing plan affecting the local manufacturing site, including the earlier closure of the penicillin department. The job reductions are expected to involve direct dismissals of permanent staff as well as the non-renewal of temporary agency contracts, while potential indirect effects on subcontractors and service providers may also arise. Updated, 20/07/2026: Workers and trade unions organised a protest outside the Catania plant on 18 July 2026, calling on Pfizer to withdraw the redundancy procedure and seeking guarantees on the future of the site ahead of discussions at the Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy (MIMIT). Capgemini, a French IT services group operating in Germany, has announced substantial job cuts across several German locations as a result of the ongoing Volkswagen crisis. The company plans to reduce its workforce at its Wolfsburg-Warmenau site from 306 employees to 74, resulting in the loss of 232 jobs, while a further 202 positions are to be cut in Munich. Entire sites in Frankfurt, Nuremberg and Gaimersheim are scheduled to close, and the workforce in Stuttgart will be reduced by half to around 79 employees. The restructuring is being driven by a sharp decline in demand from Volkswagen for Capgemini's services. Volkswagen also recently announced that they will cut 35,000 jobs in Germany by the end of 2030 Volkswagen 2024 - DE. Trade union IG Metall has organised resistance at the Wolfsburg site. The union is seeking talks with the company and aims to preserve as many jobs as possible. The full extent of the redundancies and the way in which the measures will be implemented have yet to be finalised. Capgemini employs more than 420,000 people worldwide. Porsche, a German sports car manufacturer, plans to cut up to 4,000 additional jobs as part of a comprehensive transformation package aimed at streamlining the company. The cuts will mainly affect management and administrative positions, with a significant share of the reductions expected at the Weissach development centre. The restructuring is being driven by weak sales in China and substantial investment requirements. Porsche and employee representatives are currently negotiating a detailed package of measures related to the job cuts. The agreement is expected to be finalised by the end of July 2026. The agreement extends site security at Zuffenhausen and Weissach until 2035 and earmarks €2.1 billion in investments for these two locations. IG Metall welcomed the plan and highlighted its support for employee protections and continued industrial presence in Germany. Diageo, a British alcoholic-drinks group, announced a global cost-reduction plan that will result in at least 134 job cuts and could reach up to 246 across its operations. The company plans to cut 96 jobs in Italy (Milan), 38 in Scotland and up to 150 in Ireland, mainly through direct dismissals. The cuts are part of a CEO-led initiative to reduce non-core costs, as the global alcohol industry continues to face weak demand following the post-pandemic slowdown. Against this backdrop, Diageo’s organic net sales fell by 2.8% in the first half of fiscal 2026. Social partners, including GMB Scotland, have opposed the plans, although formal negotiations have not yet begun. Diageo is a British multinational drinks company whose brands include Guinness, Baileys, Gordon's, Johnnie Walker and Smirnoff. Nowomag, a Polish manufacturer of mining machinery in Nowy Sącz, is closing its production plant by the end of the year. All 150 production and technical workers are affected. The closure follows a long-term decline in demand for mining equipment and falling order volumes. The decision is linked to challenges facing the coal mining sector, the closure of shipments to Russia and broader changes in energy markets. Further production is being consolidated within the Grenevia Group rather than relocated abroad, it will continue in the Glinik factory in Gliwice. Job cuts at Glinik are also expected. The affected workforce includes welders, fitters, CNC operators, quality controllers and electrical technicians. All employees were informed about the closure and collective redundancies. The District Labour Office in Nowy Sącz has engaged with local companies to support the redeployment of affected workers. FAMUR/Grenevia, a Polish manufacturer of machinery for the mining sector, announced restructuring affecting its production sites in Nowy Sącz and Gorlice. In Nowy Sącz, the FAMUR Nowomag branch will cease production and be closed; around 120 employees are expected to be dismissed, while the site currently employs 152 people and some designers have already been transferred. Consultations with trade unions are ongoing, and voluntary departures or redeployment may be used where possible. An exact end date has not been announced. ZSSK Cargo, a Slovak state-owned rail freight operator, announced a plan to reduce its workforce by up to 400 positions as part of an internally approved recovery plan. The cuts would target various roles across the company, including management and train driver positions. The restructuring is already underway, with the final number of affected employees to be determined through negotiations with employee representatives, alongside the final shape of the organisational changes. Economic pressures from falling freight volumes due to the war in Ukraine, rising operating costs, and a broader industry downturn underpin the decision, following a net loss of approximately €29 million last year. Some affected train drivers may be offered transfers to the company's sister passenger operator, ZSSK, which is separately facing a shortage of drivers, though such transfers are not automatic and depend on meeting professional qualifications. DreiMeister Spezialitäten, a German confectionery manufacturer, announced the dismissal of its remaining 101 employees at the beginning of July 2026 following the opening of insolvency proceedings at its Westönnen site in Werl. The company will be wound up after insolvency administrators failed to secure an investor or obtain a viable takeover offer. The shutdown was triggered by mounting financial pressures, including soaring raw-material costs during the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent energy crisis, which undermined the firm’s expansion strategy. The insolvency led to immediate dismissal of all staff. The insolvency estate is insufficient to cover wages during the notice period, meaning the workers directly became entitled to unemployment benefits. Slovalco, a Slovak aluminium producer, announced the reactivation of its Žiari nad Hronom plant, aiming to restore up to 500 jobs from the current 200. The restructuring begins in late August 2026 and will gradually bring production back to full capacity. The initial closure and subsequent reactivation are driven by energy prices, with the company's aluminium furnaces being the largest electricity consumer in Slovakia. The project includes a ten-year power purchase agreement with Vodohospodárska výstavba, which operates hydroelectric plants, together with generous state subsidies tied to emission quota repayments and favourable electricity pricing. The job creation will concentrate solely in Žiari nad Hronom, Slovakia. The company expects to bring back roughly 300 positions, bringing employment at the site from 200 to 500 as operations scale up. The plant is aiming to grow employment from the current 200 to as many as 500 if the restart is successful. TikTok, a Chinese-based technology company operating in the social media sector, announced around 300 job cuts at its Dublin office. The majority of affected roles lie within the Trust and Safety division, with additional positions in AI data services and operations also at risk. The restructuring is slated to conclude by the end of August 2026, with employees who sign the mutual termination agreement finishing work on that date. Employees are currently negotiating through a collective consultation process overseen by the Communications Workers’ Union, which has expressed concerns over fairness and transparency in the redundancies. Nestlé Hungária, a Swiss based confectionery giant, announced the closure of its Diósgyőri chocolate factory in Miskolc, which will cut approximately 250 jobs by the end of 2026. The decision came after a sustained decline in demand for seasonal confections such as chocolate bunnies and marshmallow nests, leading to markedly reduced production in recent years. Nestlé highlighted its intent to sell the plant to an independent manufacturer so that the iconic products can continue to be produced by another company. Although the majority of workers will lose their positions, the company has agreed with employee representatives to provide a special bonus and severance payments for those who remain employed until end of December. In September, Vimpex, a Hungarian group, was announced as the buyer of the plant. Vimpex has committed to retain at least one third of the workforce, from January 2027. Nestlé said it would provide assistance for those employees who are not retained by the new owner. Cobendai, a Spanish automotive dealership group, has begun issuing objective dismissal notices to its 170 employees, citing economic, organisational and productive reasons and following the collapse of negotiations over its collective redundancy process (ERE). The dismissal letters were given on the 26th of June, following months of severe financial difficulties, during which many workers accumulated three to four months of unpaid wages while the company entered pre-insolvency proceedings. Worker representatives have criticised the handling of the process and the lack of transparency, while affected employees describe the outcome as the end of decades-long careers without financial security. Hyundai has stated that it continues to work individually with affected customers to resolve outstanding cases. The situation is particularly striking given that Hyundai Spain named Cobendai its “Dealer of the Year” in 2025. Safran electronics and defense, a French subsidiary of Safran, announced the creation of up to 200 new positions at its Dijon plant in France. The expansion will double the site's output by 2029 following increased European defence orders and an investment of €20 million in new facilities. The hires will mainly be technicians in optomechanics and support staff, with recruitment starting immediately and expected to complete by the end of 2029. Currently about 480 employees work at the Dijon site, and the expansion is driven by growth in defence demands. This is part of recruitment campaigns of Safran Group in France in 2026, that had already two hirings this year: 130 new hires in Gennevilliers (Ile de France) Safran Aircraft Engines 2026 - FR and 300 new positions in Domérat (Auvergne) Safran 2026 - FR. Panariagroup Deutschland, a tile manufacturer and German subsidiary of the Italian group Panariagroup, announced the closure of its plant in Leisnig, resulting in the loss of 165 jobs at the facility, at the end of June 2026. The decision follows insolvency proceedings triggered by high energy costs and declining demand. Employees will continue to receive their wages through the state insolvency benefit scheme until the end of June. Negotiations are currently taking place between the works council and the insolvency administrator on a reconciliation of interests for the affected employees. A small number of workers have received job offers from the Meta-Wolf Group. Although the new owners, the Meta-Wolf Group and Singapore-based TWO Family Office, have acquired the premises, they decided not to take over the existing operations. Instead, they have retained the furnaces for potential future use. The future owners plan to modernise the facility and, when production resumes in 2027, invest in solar systems, robotics and artificial intelligence. This restructuring follows the 2023 reduction of 120 jobs resulting from the insolvency of Steuler Fliesengruppe. Following the insolvency, the Leisnig plant was sold to Italy's Panaria Group and became Panariagroup Deutschland. Mister Spex, a German eyewear retailer, announced the closure of its logistics and production centre in Berlin-Spandau, resulting in 125 job losses. The facility will be phased out during the second half of 2026, with the full transfer of operations to logistics partner Arvato scheduled for completion by the end of the year. The logistics function is being outsourced to Arvato, a subsidiary of Bertelsmann. The company will take over warehousing operations and the processing of returns. According to Mister Spex, the move is intended to increase efficiency and provide greater cost flexibility. The company has stated that it intends to implement the workforce reduction in a socially responsible manner and has developed a support package for affected employees. This includes financial assistance during the transition period as well as support with future career opportunities and job placement. Mister Spex employs more than 900 people. Nosoli, a French book retail group, announced the closure of 11 stores— 7 Le Furet du Nord stores and 4 Decitre shops—threatening up to 163 jobs. The affected units are libraries across France, including locations in Roubaix, Villeneuve-d'Ascq, Roissy, Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines, Plaisir, Béthune, Lyon, Grenoble and Saint-Étienne. At the end of 2025, ActuaLitté reported on Nosoli's economic difficulties, when the group injected funds to maintain Decitre's activity. In 2024, 50 jobs had already been cut and five stores closed by the Nosoli group: 3 Le Furet du Nord points of sale, in Lille, Paris and Beauvais. Nosoli operates over 600 employees across its 27 outlets. Citation Eurofound (2026), Nosoli Group, Closure in France, factsheet number 300704, European Restructuring Monitor. Walcownia Metali Dziedzice, a Polish non-ferrous metal semi-finished products manufacture announced planned collective redundancies affecting 200 employees. The planned reduction includes 163 production workers and 37 administrative employees. The restructuring is attributed to difficult conditions in the European metal processing sector and the need to adjust the company’s processes, business model and product offer to market changes. Consultations with trade unions and employee representatives are ongoing, with talks expected to define the final conditions of the redundancies. The redundancy has been reported to the public employment services. Walcownia Metali Dziedzice, a Polish brass-processing company operating in the metal manufacturing sector and owned by Boryszew Group, has agreed a collective redundancy plan affecting up to 150 production and support workers at its Czechowice-Dziedzice facility in the Silesian region. The restructuring was announced in July 2026 and the dismissals are scheduled to take place between July 2026 and February 2027. According to management, the reduction is necessary to preserve the company’s financial liquidity and adapt its operating model to challenging market conditions. The company employes 447 people. The final number of redundancies was reduced from the initially proposed 200 positions to a maximum of 150 following negotiations. Trade union representatives, including Solidarność, participated in negotiations with management regarding the planned redundancies. The negotiations resulted in an agreement limiting the number of dismissals and providing additional support for workers approaching retirement age. Indorama Ventures, a multinational chemical group, announced the closure of its production site in Steinfort, Luxembourg, on end of June 2026. The decision will eliminate roughly 100 industrial jobs at this facility. The workforce affected consists mainly of plant operators and support staff employed at the site. The shutdown reflects a strategic realignment following heavy dependence on a single client and broader market pressures. Trade unions OGBL and LCGB have have requested urgent meetings with the Luxembourg Ministers of Economy and Labour to explore job preservation options. All layoffs will occur in Steinfort; they are collective dismissals with no other measures reported. Indorama Ventures is a multinational group with an annual turnover of nearly €12 billion and production sites in over 30 countries. The Steinfort site is one of its European facilities. British American Tobacco, a British multinational tobacco manufacturer, announced the reduction of about 9,000 positions worldwide. The cuts target roles across the group’s global operations. The programme is scheduled to conclude by the end of 2026. Of the 9,000 jobs cut, 5,500 are direct redundancies, whilst 3,500 are being outsourced to Accenture and other partners. This represents a massive cutback that mainly affects administrative, financial, IT and logistics functions. The US operations, managed by the subsidiary Reynolds American, are not affected by these cuts – a strategic decision that reflects the importance of the US market to BAT. By contrast, the European (United Kingdom, Poland, Romania), Latin American (Costa Rica, Mexico) and Asian (Singapore, Malaysia) regions are bearing the brunt of the restructuring.
